# dsh-composer-plus

> Composer Plus: a community plugin for DeepSeek Harness (dsh), DeepSeek's open-source agent harness. One install adds Codex-style quality-of-life features to the dsh desktop app and web UI, and iPhone access with the Tether app. npm package: `dsh-composer-plus`. MIT license. Unofficial.

Install in the dsh desktop app: Settings → Plugins → Add plugin → `dsh-composer-plus` → Enable now. Install in a web/CLI profile: `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-composer-plus`, then restart dsh. Requires dsh >= 0.2.0-rc.2 and Node.js >= 22. Tested on dsh 0.2.2-rc.5 (web). The desktop app was not tested on this version.

Features (each one can be switched off in Settings → Composer Plus):

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED FEATURES: edit docs/features.json, then run npm run build:readme -->
- Changes panel: right sidebar page that opens on a branch map of the chat's repository (counts of all, merged and waiting branches that filter the map; each branch colored by whether the main branch has its work, with an arrow to the branch that merged it or that it started from; remote branches only without a local branch of the same name; a branch opens its newest 300 commits, a commit its files and diffs, the Merged label the merge commit, the Waiting label the files that the branch brings into its target), uncommitted / unstaged / staged / branch git changes and per-file diffs, a "This chat" view (the files that the open chat's file tools wrote in all its turns, with their total diff since its first message) and a switch that hides whitespace-only changes (`git diff -w`); a file's menu lists the chats of the same repository whose write/edit tools changed that file (newest first, with the request; read from the chat logs, rolled-back requests marked) and opens a chat at that request; read-only git.
- Feature ideas: Tinder-style cards on a right sidebar page; on a click, the chat's own model reads a short read-only summary of the project (top-level names, README/manifest heads, an outline of the rest of the README, the titles of recent commits; no .env or key files, no symlink out of the project, no FIFO) and suggests up to 8 features as swipeable cards, written in dsh's UI language. Swipe right (✓ or →) starts a new chat in the same project in plan mode with the idea; ▶ Build now (or ↑) starts the new chat without plan mode, so the model makes the change at once (usual approvals); swipe left (✕ or ←) skips; ↓ (button or key) saves the idea in the project's Later list (kept per project folder under the dsh home, also after a restart; at most 50), where Plan starts the same plan-mode chat and Build now the chat without a plan, and both remove it from the list; Plan all (N) starts one plan-mode chat for every idea in the list and empties it; History keeps every suggested idea of the project (skipped, saved, started; at most 200) and the model never gets them again (Forget allows one again); the buttons and keys fly the card off like a swipe; Undo (Z) brings a card back. An optional focus topic (free text, at most 80 characters, or the fixed chips Performance, Accessibility, Tests, Security, Usability, Documentation) limits the suggestions to that topic; an empty focus sends the same request as before. Copy as checklist (Later list) copies the saved ideas as a Markdown checklist (`- [ ] Title — Summary`) with no network call. Open GitHub issue (Later list) runs the user's own `gh issue create` in the project folder (the gh login of the Mac, the project's GitHub remote) with the idea's title and summary, and keeps the issue link on the idea. No model call before the click; nothing in the project is written.
- Content search: On by default; applies after a dsh restart. The dsh sidebar search (magnifier next to Workspaces, Cmd+K in the desktop app, Cmd+Alt+K in a browser) also finds chats by words in user and assistant messages and shows the matching text. It switches on dsh's built-in SQLite FTS5 index (off in shipped dsh) with an owner-only file at `$DSH_HOME/cache/composer-plus/session-search.db`; no own search code. Whole words only, no tool output; the first search after a start builds the index (about 15 s and about 1 GB peak Host memory for 250 chats).
- Turn rollback: Like OpenCode's undo or Claude Code's /rewind, a ↶ button on each of your messages takes that message and everything after it out of the chat and the model context (one hidden marker, the same mechanism as dsh's /compact; the log is never rewritten) and puts the message back in the composer to edit and resend. "Chat and files" also puts the project files back as they were before that message, bash changes too: the Host takes a git snapshot of the work tree before each message into a private store under `$DSH_HOME/cache/composer-plus/rollback/` (the repository's objects are read, never written; index, HEAD, refs, stash and config are untouched); only regular files inside the chat folder are written. Needs a git repository for files; the 50 newest snapshots per chat. When dsh-rewind-plugin is installed it owns rollback and Composer Plus shows no button. After a rollback, Redo starts a new chat from just before it (dsh's own fork, the same model context) and can put the files back; a file edited after the rollback is kept unless you choose to overwrite it.
- Delete chat: "Delete…" in a chat's sidebar menu (dsh itself only archives). The chat stops (dsh's own archive with stop) and its log folders, with its subagent chats, move to the macOS Trash (elsewhere `$DSH_HOME/trash`); the id stays archived, so a folder put back shows up under "Archived only" after a restart.
- Project name in the composer: the stats row under the composer (turns, tokens, cache hit) starts with the chat's project name (dsh's project title, else the folder name); the folder path is its tooltip; a click finds the chat in the sidebar (opens the sidebar, the project and Show more, scrolls to the chat, which blinks for 5 seconds).
- Input history: ↑ / ↓ in an empty composer recalls messages you sent.
- Shift+Tab plan mode: Shift+Tab adds or removes `/plan ` at the start of the draft, or leaves plan mode.
- Keep composer focus: after you send a `/` command or skill, the cursor goes back to the composer, unless a menu, a dialog or another field has the focus. (dsh makes the composer read-only while it resolves the command, and the browser removes the focus.)
- Fit question card to window: dsh's question card (`ask_user_question`) scrolls the question and its answers together, keeps Skip and Submit in view at the bottom, and uses the height of the window less 200 px. Without it, dsh caps the card at 60% of the window (at most 520 px) and scrolls only the answers, so a long question can push its own end, the answers and the buttons out of the card. On dsh 0.2.2+ dsh fits the card itself (question preview with Expand): NATIVE_FEATURES detects it by the `question` dictionary key `text.expand`, so the feature is off by default there (an explicit choice stays) and its Settings row shows the note settings.nativeNote (role note).
- Fit chat header to window: in a narrow window, dsh's chat header buttons (mode, subagents, background jobs, Open in, the branch pill, the grants chip) move to a second line instead of covering each other, and the chat title keeps at least 120 px. A wide window keeps dsh's own one-line header.
- Remember window size: the desktop app opens its window with the size and place that it had last time, not at dsh's fixed 1280 × 820. Saved per computer in the app's own storage; only in the desktop app.
- Codex dark theme: off by default, browser-only switch. While dsh shows its dark palette (body[data-ds-dark-theme]), one style element sets dsh's --dsw-* color tokens to a neutral set: chat #141414, sidebar #1C1C1C (macOS vibrancy kept, tint 82% neutral, no blue/violet wash), right panel #181818, bubbles and composer #292929, selected row #303030, borders #2B2B2B, text #EAE8E4 / #A09F9B / muted #A3A29E (4.5:1 on every surface and its hover fills), dsh's business blue (tab, caret, focus ring, links, Stop circle) → off-white, success sage #A3B68C, warn amber #DCAE66, waiting sand #E2D9BC, error unchanged. Only color properties (plus a link underline and a 2 px focus-ring offset on off-white buttons). Composer Plus's own blue and violet accents (board, branch list, Questions callout) become neutral too. Off removes the style: dsh's own colors at once. The light palette never changes.
- Running subagents in the chat header: dsh's subagent counter in the chat header shows the subagents that run now (also 0) instead of all the subagents that the chat ever had. The open list shows the total on its first line and the running subagents first. Switched off, dsh's own counter (the total) shows again.
- One-click Continue: after a stopped, failed or cut-off turn the Send button becomes ▶ and resumes without a visible chat message. Queued messages stay queued: ▶ continues only the stopped task, then the queue runs.
- Resume after restart: Off by default. Chats that were working when dsh quit or closed continue by themselves at the next start; a running `/goal` round goes on with the next goal round. Chats you stopped, finished or failed chats do not continue. dsh has no built-in setting for this.
- Resume after an AIProxy outage: On by default (the Host keeps the switch and the UI language in outage-resume.json). When a top-level chat's turn on an AIProxy provider ends with AIProxy's `499 request_cancelled` or the transport's `Connection error.` (not a user stop, a denied approval or another error), failures within 60 s count as one outage. The Host asks AIProxy's `GET /health` (http://127.0.0.1:21028, or COMPOSER_PLUS_HEALTH_URL) every second; after at least one failed check (a Connection error counts as one) and 10 s of good checks; a 499 while AIProxy stays up (a request cancelled in its window) continues nothing, each failed chat that did not move on gets one message in the UI language through dsh's prompt (as chat_send): "The turn stopped because of an AIProxy outage. Continue from where you stopped; do not repeat the steps that you completed." At most one message per chat per outage and two per chat per hour. dsh's notice of a subagent that failed this way gets one more line for the parent agent that names the outage. The Assistant status panel marks each continued chat in its Tasks list and counts the other continued chats in one line, without names or links. AIProxy's 429, 500 or 503 upstream_rejected or 504 upstream_timeout before the answer starts (the provider refused the request or did not answer in time; AIProxy runs) skips the health check: the chat gets the same message 3 min (OUTAGE.retry) after its newest refusal, in the same limit (two per chat per hour, outages and refusals together), so dsh also starts the chat's queued messages; a user stop gets nothing.
- Queue drag-and-drop: reorder queued messages by dragging the ⠿ grip or with ↑ / ↓.
- Edit queued message in place: double-click a queued message or click its Edit button to edit it in place: change the text, remove images and files (✕) or add new ones (paperclip or paste). Enter saves, Esc cancels, Shift+Enter adds a line. The message keeps its place in the queue, and the kept images and files stay as they are. The queue cannot be reordered while the editor is open. In Tether: queued message menu → Edit (a sheet).
- Send after Stop goes first: on by default. After you stop a chat that has queued messages, a message that you send runs at once and alone; the queued messages keep their order and run after it, one per turn. Without it, dsh puts the new message at the end of the queue and runs the first queued message instead (a dsh queue issue).
- Copy session link: right-click a chat to copy a `dsh-session:` link that attaches it to another chat as read-only context. dsh 0.2.1's own "Copy Session ID" copies only the plain id; this item comes right after it.
- Copy message link: a 🔗 button on each message copies `dsh-session:<chat>#<message seq>`; sent in a chat (dsh 0.2.1 and later), the link is a chip that opens that chat, loads its history back to the message, scrolls to it and highlights it. dsh still attaches the linked chat as read-only context.
- Export chat as Markdown: right-click a chat (or its … menu) → Export as Markdown… → Copy to clipboard or Save .md file. The user's messages and the assistant's text replies, oldest first, with a title, the project name and the date; code blocks are kept (an open fence is closed); tool calls, thinking, hidden context and messages withdrawn by Turn rollback or dsh-rewind-plugin are left out (messages that /compact summarized stay); at most about 4 million characters. The Host route `GET /api/composer-plus.export?sessionId=` reads only the chat log.
- Copy project path: right-click a project in the sidebar → Copy path copies its full folder path.
- Project search in a new chat: the new chat project menu lists the projects A–Z and has a search box (type part of a name, Enter picks the first match); dsh's saved project order does not change.
- Default workspace for New session: the global New session button (the sidebar top button, its shortcut, the logo) always opens in one default workspace, set in Settings (a project of dsh, or dsh's general folder Documents/deepseek-harness/default-workspace, made on first use), not in the open or the most recent project; a project's own "+" and the new chat project menu still choose any project; the Tether iPhone app's Quick chat uses the same default.
- Find in chat: Cmd+F on macOS (Ctrl+F on Windows and Linux) opens a find box over the open chat: every match in the messages and replies that the page shows is highlighted (CSS Custom Highlight API, dsh's DOM is not changed), with n / total, next and previous (Enter, Shift+Enter, ↓, ↑, wrap-around) and Esc to close; case, accents and the Turkish dotless ı are ignored; it follows a streaming reply. Closed tool steps and history that is not loaded are not searched.
- Branch per chat: each chat can run on its own git branch: on the new chat screen the branch button (branch icon) between the project button and the mode button starts on New branch (in the main folder of a repository with a commit; Current branch can still be chosen), and the first message (it can carry images and files) makes the AI name the branch (a message with no text gets the dated name feat/chat-YYYYMMDD-HHMM, with no model call), creates a worktree in <project>/.worktrees/, copies the files listed in .worktreeinclude (for example .env and node_modules, never other ignored files) and opens a new chat there with the text, the images and the files; in plan mode (`/plan <message>`, or a new chat already in plan mode) the new branch chat starts in plan mode with the message; the composer takes no text while the branch is created; the open chat's header shows its branch, changes and push state.
- Branches in the workspace tree: off by default: each branch with a worktree folder in <project>/.worktrees/ shows as a project inside its project (dsh's Workspace Tree view nests it), a branch whose folder is deleted leaves the list and its chats go to Ungrouped; when the agent of a chat in the project folder creates and checks out a branch while the folder has no uncommitted changes, the project folder goes back to its branch, the branch gets its own worktree folder, and the chat moves there (a copy continues the task in the branch project, the old chat is archived); checked at start, every 30 s, after each turn and on window focus.
- Next message prediction: On by default; switch it off in Settings. After a finished turn, the empty composer shows a guess of the user's next message in that chat (Tab accepts, Esc hides); the model is chosen in Settings from dsh's own model list, default = dsh's default model; one short model call per finished turn; Tether shows it above the composer.
- Complete while typing: Off by default; switch it on in Settings. While the user types, grey text after the cursor shows how the message may go on (Tab adds it, Esc hides it); it suggests only the user's own next words (never a reply to the user, no made-up error texts or names) and shows nothing when the message looks complete or the model is not sure; its own Model menu in Settings (default: Same as Next message prediction; the choice is kept by the Host in complete.json and a model must be one that dsh lists); one model call at each pause while typing (many more tokens); not for slash commands, chips or a cursor that is not at the end; Tether shows it above the field (tap adds it).
- Improve prompt: On by default (a model call only on a click). A magic wand button in the composer's tool row rewrites the typed draft as a clearer prompt for the agent (goal first, numbered steps for several parts, the check to run), with this chat (rolled-back messages left out), the project brief (README, AGENTS.md, manifests, latest commits), git's changed files and the paths whose names match the draft as context; keeps the draft's language and never invents names. The result replaces the draft in the composer and is not sent; Cmd/Ctrl+Z (one step) or the Undo improvement button brings the typed text back; typing during the call keeps the new text; Esc or a second click cancels; one call per chat at a time. Its own Model menu in Settings (default: the chat's model; kept by the Host in improve.json, a model must be one that dsh lists). A `/goal <objective>` (or `/goal edit <objective>`) draft gets its own rules: only the objective is rewritten, as a checkable completion condition (outputs, checks, evidence shown in the chat, unresolved parts marked, stop on a lasting blocker), and the command as typed stays in front (also a command chip). Not for other slash commands or a draft with a file chip; at most 8000 characters. Tether has the wand next to the field. With Project memory on (and not off for this chat), up to about 4000 characters of memory notes of the project and the global memory (Project memory's own store: the notes that share words with the draft first, then the newest of the main files) go along as data; a note or chat message that looks like a key or password, and any path under a folder named Gizli, are never read or sent.
- Goal check: On by default (a model call only when the agent marks a goal complete; it never starts a turn). When the model calls update_goal with action complete in an automatic /goal round, the Host (tools/pre-execute, after every other gate allowed it) first runs the project's test command (the chat's own command, else detected: package.json scripts.test with npm/pnpm/yarn/bun by lock file, Makefile test, cargo test, go test ./..., pytest; project files read only as regular files inside the chat folder) under the chat's sandbox mode; it skips the run when the agent's newest change-capable step was its own passing bash run of that exact command in the same folder (a pipe or && does not count). Then one verifier model call with no tools and a fresh context reads the goal, the chat since the goal started (rolled-back steps left out), git status and the test result, and answers an evidence table (`items: [{item, verdict: verified|incorrect|unresolved, evidence, fix}]`; pass only when every item is verified (every row counts, also a nameless one or one after the 20th, which are not shown); an older `{pass, missing}` answer still parses). The deny text lists each open item with its evidence and fix; the row shows "N of M verified" with the table in its tooltip. A failed test (no model call then), a verifier 'not done' or a check error denies the call with the reason: the goal stays active and dsh's goal driver starts the next round. A human turn, /goal and the goal bar are not checked. Optional per-chat time and token budget (tokens include the chat's subagent chats, any depth, since the budget started): over it, the goal becomes blocked (code budget-limit) at the next idle edge; resuming starts a new budget. A row under dsh's goal bar shows the test, the last result and the budget, with Edit, Run now and Clear. Its own Model menu in Settings (default: the chat's model). Kept by the Host in goal-check.json. Not in Tether (the check runs on the Mac).
- Continue in a new chat: On by default (a model call only on a click). A chat's … menu (or right-click) → Continue in a new chat…: one call to the chat's own model writes a handoff note from the chat's own events (a fork's copied events and steps withdrawn by Turn rollback or dsh-rewind left out; tool calls and the end of their results are evidence) with the sections Task, Outputs, Completed, Decisions, Open issues, Next action. The note opens in an editable dialog (Write again, Start new chat, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter); Start new chat makes a new chat in the same project (its sidebar group) whose first message is the note plus a `dsh-session:` link to the old chat (dsh attaches it as read-only context), and opens it; when the message cannot be sent, the new chat is archived (all or none). A newer note stops the older call, so a closed dialog never locks the chat; a start is refused while a note runs and runs to its end (Host 409 for a second one). Nothing is written to the project. Tether: chat title menu → Continue in a new chat.
- Context breakdown: On by default (no model call). Right sidebar → + → Context: what fills the open chat's model context now, from its log only. The surface is rebuilt as dsh does (append; a replace of a range by /compact, Turn rollback, dsh-rewind or a new system prompt), and each part is priced with dsh's token-meter rule (4 characters per token, +4 per block and per message): system prompt, project instructions (AGENTS.md), skills, your messages, agent replies and tool calls, tool results by tool, MCP results by server, tool definitions of the newest request (dsh / mcp: <server>), compact summary, other context notes and rollback markers, each with tokens and the share of the context window (from dsh's request/context). A click on a part lists its tools or servers. It reads again after each turn and on Refresh. The Host route `GET /api/composer-plus.context?sessionId=` reads only the chat log. Tether: chat title menu → Context.
- Planned steps: Off by default (it runs commands without a new model call; the Host keeps the switch in planned-steps.json). After HarnessMM (arXiv 2610.32813, guarded decision reuse). While on, every chat gets the tool plan_next_steps({steps: [{id, after: root|<earlier id>, when: ok|always, tool: bash|read|grep|glob, arguments}]}) (1–8 steps, arguments ≤ 8 KB, no background bash) and a short prompt section. An llm/stream listener reads each agent request's messages (stateless): when the newest model message holds an accepted plan, its other tool calls (root) and the steps already run all have results, and exactly one step is ready (predecessor done; ok = not an error result and, for bash, no dsh fail mark such as [exit code: N] in the last 8 lines), Composer Plus answers that request itself with one assistant message: a reasoning block (only when the planning message had one: DeepSeek thinking mode needs it in the history), a text line "Composer Plus · Planned steps: ran `<id>` … without a model call" and the step's tool call (id cpgs-<8 hex>-<n>). dsh runs the call on its normal path (tools/pre-execute: approval, sandbox, Protected files). No ready step, two ready steps, a failed guard, the last step, any user message (user, steer, Continue, /compact, rollback) or a request with a purpose (compaction) → the model. Restart, fork, rollback and /compact need no state: the plan is in the request history. AIProxy chats (17 Nov 2026: AIProxy's Claude Code bridge pins the tool call ids of its own last answer, so a step message makes it answer 409 session_mismatch for that chat): the tool is registered with dsh's step condition when (dsh 0.2.2+) that leaves it out when the step's modelSelection.provider is AIProxy (route id or display name matches /aiproxy/i, as Resume after an AIProxy outage), the section is empty for that selection (else the agent's options provider, dsh before 0.2.2), the listener answers no step when GenerateOptions.provider is AIProxy (an older plan too: it goes to the model), and the tool refuses when the agent's newest request went to AIProxy (dsh before 0.2.2 has no when). Other providers keep it all. Not in Tether (a Mac setting).
- Advisor model: Off by default (each use is a paid call of another model; the Host keeps everything in advisor.json). After Claude Code's advisor tool (issue #8). While on and with an advisor model chosen, every chat gets the tool advisor() (no arguments, no prompt section). A call makes one tool-free model call to the chosen provider/model (optional reasoning effort when the model lists it; maxTokens 1000–64000, default 16000, never above the model default; 5 min timeout) with a short advisor system prompt and one user message: the start of the newest system prompt (6000 characters), the tool names of the newest request header and the chat log as text (goalTranscript: withdrawn steps out, the newest 100000 characters kept, the cut said in the text; withoutSecrets drops secret-looking lines). Plain text, never the raw provider request (a provider can refuse tool history without tools or without reasoning blocks). The result: "Advice from <model> (<n> input tokens, <n> output tokens; use <k> of <max> in this chat):" and the advice; the client draws it as an Advice row (tool.call.toolview). Limits: uses per chat (1–20, default 3) counted from the chat's own successful advisor results (a fork starts at inheritedEventCount), one call at a time per chat; at the limit the tool returns an error and makes no call. Subagents (unless allowed) and chats that the user switched off (chat header button, POST {sessionId, off}) get the tool removed with dsh's per-agent tools.restrict (dsh 0.2.0+; register(def, {when}) exists only from 0.2.2) and the tool refuses there. dsh's usage meter does not count the advisor's tokens, and Composer Plus does not ask for provider prompt caching. Not in Tether (a Mac setting; the advice shows as a tool result in the phone's chat).
- Turkish skill pack: On by default, only while the dsh UI language is Turkish (tr, tr-*). The client posts the active locale id to the Host (POST /api/composer-plus.turkish-skill {lang}; a Settings click sends {on, lang}); the Host keeps {on, lang} in turkish-skill.json. While on and Turkish, the Host asks api.github.com for the newest commit of yucezerey/turkish-anti-ai-skill (MIT) at most once a day, reads the recursive git tree of that commit and downloads from raw.githubusercontent.com only the regular (mode 100644) .md files under skills/turkish-anti-ai-skill/ with plain relative names (no dot files, no '..', ≤ 20 files, ≤ 256 KB each, ≤ 1 MB total); each file must hash to its git blob id in the tree; SKILL.md must name turkish-anti-ai-skill. The copy goes to $DSH_HOME/cache/composer-plus/turkish-skill/<commit> (owner-only, written in a temporary folder and renamed; older copies removed) and is registered with ctx.skills.register as a runtime skill (resourceBase: that folder; dsh's skill tool loads it on demand). No script of the pack runs. Another language unregisters it (the copy stays); off unregisters it and deletes the copy. A failed check keeps the copy in use and shows the reason in Settings. Not in Tether (a Mac setting).
- Untangle codebase: On by default (the Host keeps the switch in untangle-codebase.json). Registers one dsh skill provider, `composer-plus` (ctx.skills.registerProvider, in a ctx.inject(['skills']) fiber), with one skill: untangle-codebase, the unchanged SKILL.md of caldoai/skills commit f3cf477 (MIT, © 2026 Maze), shipped with its LICENSE in assets/skills/untangle-codebase/; no network call. invocation {modelInvocable: false, userInvocable: true}: dsh lists it in the `/` menu and in skills/list, and injects its body (with the text after the command as the focus) when a user message has `/untangle-codebase`, but the model's skill catalog leaves it out, so it adds no prompt tokens to other chats. rank 600 (dsh's BUNDLED_SKILL_RANK): a project, custom or user skill with the same name wins. The skill itself runs as a /goal: it asks about the optional comment and test cleanup, lists hidden links, needless links, surplus and special cases, redesigns, fixes and re-checks with subagents. Switch off disposes the provider: the next catalog has no entry and `/untangle-codebase` is plain text. In Tether: the phone sends the text and the Mac injects the skill.
- Protected files: On by default (the Host keeps the switch and the list in protected-files.json). A tools/pre-execute gate, after every other gate allowed the call, denies dsh's file tools (also a call that would otherwise ask the user) for paths that match the user's glob patterns: read, read_image and grep with a file path ("read and write" patterns), write, edit and str_replace_editor (both modes; its view reads). Defaults: .env*, *.pem, *.key (read and write). The default .env* does not cover env templates (basename .env.example or .env.<name>.example, exact case) when the real path that the file tool uses has that name and is a regular file with one hard link, or a new file; a link with a template name to a file that is not a template (for example .env), a file with more than one hard link, a ~/ path that dsh 0.2.2+ reads from the home folder and resolves to such a file, .env.example.bak, .env.example~ and .env.local stay protected; a pattern of the user still covers a template. A pattern without / matches a file name at any depth; ** any folders; a folder pattern (secrets/) covers everything in it; a leading ./ is dropped; case is ignored; the match is linear in time (no regex); the real path counts too (a symlink to a protected file is protected). The deny text tells the agent not to use another tool and to ask the user. Not covered: bash and other shells, scripts, MCP tools, glob listings and folder-wide grep. Settings → Protected files: the list (add, remove, read and write / write only, Use the defaults). Not in Tether (a Mac setting).
- Blocked commands: On by default with an empty list (the Host keeps the switch and the list in blocked-commands.json; after dsh-superagent's blockedCommands). A tools/pre-execute gate, after every other gate, reads the command of dsh's `bash` and `pwsh` calls: a "block" rule denies the call (also one that would ask) with a reason that tells the agent not to run it another way and to ask the user; an "ask first" rule turns an allowed call into dsh's approval card (its reason never starts like an Auto review ask, so Allow for this chat does not answer it; in a chat whose approval policy is never it is a deny); a denied or cancelled call stays so. A rule is a command name (any word of a simple command, so after sudo, env or timeout too; the last path part, case ignored, .exe/.cmd/.bat/.com dropped) and words that must follow in that order, other words between allowed; `*` any text (a `*` in the command too, so `rm *` matches `rm *.log`), `?` one character. The scanner splits on ; & | ( ) newlines and { }, knows quotes and escapes, reads $(…) and backticks as commands, skips # comments and here-document text (a here-document read by a shell, an unquoted one's $(…), and the text of sh/bash/zsh -c (also after other options: -c -x, -c --, -o pipefail -c), pwsh -Command (any prefix: -c, -co, --command, /c) and -CommandWithArgs/-cwa, eval, iex and a here-string to a shell are read again, 3 levels); linear in time. Not covered: a variable or alias that names the command, a function, a script file, another interpreter (python -c), MCP tools, your own terminal. Settings → Blocked commands: the list (add, remove, block / ask first). Not in Tether (a Mac setting; an ask first approval shows in Tether's approval sheet).
- Task board: On by default (the Host keeps the switch in board-switch.json and the record of the board's chats and the chats taken off the board in board-chats.json, owner-only, under storages/dsh-composer-plus). A kanban board of dsh's real chats, after Kanzo (github.com/emanuele-em/kanzo, AGPL-3.0; no code of it is used). Left sidebar → Task board, or Cmd+Shift+K (Ctrl+Shift+K) anywhere in dsh, also in the composer (a dsh shortcut command composerPlus.taskBoard: the user can change it on dsh's Keyboard shortcuts page; dsh refuses a default that another command has, then the command comes without a key; no web Linux default; gone with the feature switch): the board has the full width (no project column); the project name at the top of the board is a button that opens the project list as a dropdown over the columns: the search box, the filter, All projects and the projects (dsh workspaces; a Branch per chat folder <repo>/.worktrees/<name> counts as its repository) with their running and waiting counts; columns Doing, Review, Done (no Todo). A project with a waiting chat has dsh's orange dot in the list (its counts as text for screen readers), and the closed button has the dot while any chat waits. A pick, Enter in the search box (the first project that the list shows; an empty box or no match does nothing), Esc (a full search box empties first), Tab out of the list and a press outside it close it; a closed list forgets its search. The search box, the filter and All projects stay in place; only the project list scrolls. In a narrow board the header stays on one line (the counts line hides first). Every top-level chat shows (not archived or subagent chats; a blank chat only as the open New task), from dsh's own client stores: a pending approval, question or plan review → Review (orange dot), running or a running subagent → Doing, else finished. Done has only the unread finished chats (green: dsh's unread dot, or the board's own in-memory set of chats that finished while they were dsh's open chat behind a panel, such as a New task behind the board, until that chat shows with no panel over it, runs again or goes; layout.panelInfo + retainedBy.mainView; gone with the switch); newest first, 50 (Show N older). A card that you read leaves Done by itself: a row Recently finished (N) under the unread cards opens the read ones in place (10 newest, then Show N older; open or closed kept per device in localStorage dsh-composer-plus.board.recentDone, closed by default); the Done count counts the unread cards. Each Done card has an × that takes it off the board, and the Done column head has Clear all only while Recently finished is open: a dialog first names the count and the project (or all projects), says that the chats stay in dsh and how many unread cards stay; then every read Done card of the shown project (also the older ones; an unread green card stays) goes. POST board-chats {hide: [ids]} adds them to the Host's list (merged, at most 5,000, kept after a restart; a chat that runs at that moment is not added). After each removal, Undo shows for 8 s; Removed (N) under Done opens a panel of the removed cards of the shown project (newest 100, then Show N older) with Put back; both send POST board-chats {unhide: [ids]} (an id that is not on the list writes nothing). No chat is deleted or changed in dsh. A hidden chat is left out of Done only; when it runs again (agent/status running) the Host takes it off the list, so its card comes back. One change of the list (hide, Undo, Put back, Clear all's confirm) at a time in every entry point; the cards move at once, a failure moves them back with its reason. An older Host half (no hidden list) shows none of them. The project list has a search box (every word in the name; case, accents and Turkish dotless i ignored) and "Active in the last 2 hours" (a project with a waiting, running, unread or 2-hour-recent chat; per device). A card title has the card's full width (the time is on the tag row), so a narrow column breaks it only between words. New task (n) opens dsh's own New session (uiWorkspace.startSession) in the shown project (All projects: dsh's own pick), so the first message is written in dsh's composer (attachments, commands, model menu); POST board-chats {sessionId} records that chat with an empty prompt. Until its first message it is the first card of Doing as "New task" (a click opens it). When dsh's list shows it not blank any more, the board panel opens again by itself (once, only for that chat). The Host takes the chat's first own user message (after a fork's inherited events, not a withdrawn one) as the card's prompt, once; dsh's session-title service names the chat; one background call to the chat's model (its selection, else dsh's default; lowest effort, at most 200 tokens, 60 s, the message's first 4,000 characters) writes up to 3 tags. A card click (or Enter) opens its chat; on an orange card it opens the Answer panel instead (aria-haspopup dialog; the panel has Open chat). Answer on an orange card: approval Reject / Allow once, plan review (the plan; Approve, or Request changes with an optional note), questions (options, multi-select, own text); one answer at a time; a request that changed or was answered elsewhere is not answered again. The page reads board-chats every 2 s while it shows (only a newer rev). No drag and drop, no agent tools, no prompt section. The old notebook board.json is not read or changed. Progress on hover: a card in Doing shows a box after 400 ms of hover (at once on keyboard focus; Esc closes): the time since its turn started, the step of its todo list, the tool call that runs now or the last one and the agent's last line, read from the chat's own log every 2 s (GET board-progress); Settings → Task board → Progress on hover: Fast (no AI, the default) or AI summary (also one or two sentences from one short call to the chat's model: lowest effort, at most 200 tokens, 30 s, the chat's own newest 6,000 characters (earlier turns too: user messages, agent replies, tool calls and the end of their results); a new call only after a new step and 20 s). Tether: chat title menu → Task board (in Done a swipe takes a card off, the ⋯ menu has Clear all with a confirmation (unread cards stay) and Removed with Put back, and Undo shows for 8 s; the same list; a running card has one progress line; opens on Review when a chat waits for you, else Doing; the project list has the orange dot).
- Assistant: On by default (a missing or broken switch file reads as on; an explicit off stays off; no chat, folder or project until the first click; its tools start a turn in another chat only after the user allows it on dsh's approval card; in dsh's Auto permission mode, Auto review decides instead); the Host keeps the switch in assistant-switch.json and the chat id in assistant.json (owner-only). After DS Bot's Main Bot (Fei2411/DS-Bot, Apache-2.0; no code used). Left sidebar → Damon (sidebar.panellist, order 21, right under Task board; the row always stays: its glyph draws a style rule that hides dsh 0.2.2's Unpin button (_panelUnpin) in its own _panelEntry only, so dsh's in-memory unpin cannot remove it; other rows keep the button) → GET /api/composer-plus.assistant (only while on) gives the one assistant chat: the saved id (unarchived when archived), else mkdir ~/Assistant, workspaceRegistry.create(~/Assistant, "Assistant") (then titled Damon), sessionController.create, permission preset workspace-write, dsh's default model (no model change); a missing or deleted chat is made again; one start at a time. A short row panel shows "Opening…" until dsh's openSession shows the chat. Setup (optional: the memory never waits for it; 17 Nov 2026, the owner does not want Obsidian): GET /api/composer-plus.assistant-setup checks the disk only: Obsidian's app in its default folders (macOS /Applications and ~/Applications; Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs, %LOCALAPPDATA% and %ProgramFiles%; Linux /usr/bin, /opt, Snap, Flatpak) or, on Windows and Linux only, its obsidian.json (on macOS it stays after an uninstall), the vault list in obsidian.json (the real path of the assistant folder is a vault or inside one; no folder name is fixed, so a renamed folder that ~/Assistant links to passes), Project memory on with its active memory folder in that vault (a saved one that works after the next start: restart), and a non-empty AGENTS.md in the assistant folder. Until ready, the client shows a setup card in conversation.input.dock of the assistant chat (also after the first message; Hide closes it on this device, localStorage dsh-composer-plus.assistant.setup-hidden; while it is hidden, a button with the card title under the Assistant switch in Settings shows it again) with each step, Obsidian's official download link (https://obsidian.md/download), Set up (POST {fix: {name, dirs?: {global, projects}}}: memory folder <assistant folder>/<name in the UI language> unless the saved one is in the vault; a new memory folder gets subfolders named in the UI language (assistant.setup.globalDir, assistant.setup.projectsDir), a folder that has its subfolders keeps their names (never renamed); memory on, AGENTS.md from a template only when missing) and Check again; nothing is downloaded or installed. Without Obsidian or its vault, the assistant chat and its subagents save, change and remove notes (memory_remember, memory_forget, the review, the import) in the memory folder in use, as every chat does (the normal project memory folder unless Memory folder names another); with a ready vault, the memory folder is in the vault. Memory import: when the setup is ready or hidden, the welcome card adds a text field with the ready prompt in the UI language (assistant.import.prompt), which the user can change; Start sends it through dsh's conversation.send (nothing runs without the click). The card shows also in an assistant chat that already has messages (an update) until Start sends the prompt or the user clicks Hide; that choice is kept in the Host (POST /api/composer-plus.assistant-setup {importEnded: true} writes memory-import-card.json; GET answers importEnded, which is also true once memory-import.json has a finished file) and in localStorage (dsh-composer-plus.assistant.import; an older click there is sent to the Host), so a page with new browser storage (the other Mac's page in a Remote computers window gets new storage at each dsh start) does not show it again. Only subagents of the assistant chat get two tools, with or without Obsidian (both refuse in a chat with Project memory switched off for it): memory_import_sources({offset?}) lists and reads the documented agent memory files (user: <dsh home>/AGENTS.md, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/projects/*/memory/*.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md; each dsh project: AGENTS.md, AGENTS.local.md, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .cursorrules, .windsurfrules, .cursor/rules, .windsurf/rules, memory-bank) with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, at most 64 kB a file and 48 kB of text a page, only regular files whose real path stays in the project, never .env, key or credential files, the memory folder or the vault's Gizli/Private folder, and cuts secret-looking lines (looksSecret, a value after password/secret/api_key/_token, a secret-shaped value after a bare key/auth/token, a connection string with a password, a Bearer, Basic or Token auth header (any case after an Authorization header name, with a digit, a base64 sign or mixed case; a placeholder such as $TOKEN or <your-token> stays), TOKEN=/KEY=/AUTH= in capitals with a digit or mixed case, command-line passwords; each value is tested in code, so a long line stays linear); a dsh project in a branch worktree folder (<repo>/.worktrees/<name>) is skipped (its repository counts); a file that an earlier import finished (memory_import done; the day goes into memory-import.json, owner-only; when that file is missing, it is made once from the sources that saved notes name, so an older import counts too; while that fails, done marks nothing) and whose last change is not after that day is not read again and is listed in alreadyImported, so a run that stopped half way reads its files again; memory_import({facts: [{text, source, project?}], done?: [source]}) saves at most 50 facts per call in one save of the memory store (all or none, one history copy per memory; add: format, same-entry dedupe, journal actor import, meta source "import <path>" and the store's own added date) to the project memory of a known dsh project or the global memory; a source must be one of the files that memory_import_sources lists (else unclear); done marks only listed files, after the facts are saved (a failed save marks none); facts or done is required; it answers {added, duplicate, secret, unclear, perProject, done?}; nothing is overwritten or removed. Onboarding: while the chat that the row opened in this window has no message (SessionSnapshot.blank, no promptAttempted, not running), a card in conversation.input.dock (order 1) says what the assistant does with three example requests (a reminder, background research, your other chats and the approval card); it goes with the first message and with the switch (its style is inside the card). Six tools only in the assistant agent's own tool scope (agent.ctx.tools.register; its subagents get tools.restrict deny; each tool also refuses any other caller): chats_list({project?, status?: running|waiting_for_user|idle, limit?}) root chats of all projects (no archived, blank, subagent or the assistant itself; waiting = an open approval/asked or an open ask_user_question/exit_plan_mode call in the running turn); chat_read({chat_id, count?}) the newest user and agent messages, rollback-withdrawn messages (composer-plus-rollback and dsh-rewind) and a fork's inherited events left out, marked as data, and as the last item (role assistant) what the chat asks now: [question] header, question and options of an open ask_user_question card (also a timed one still open after its timeout or after a dsh restart, as dsh's question fold keeps it), [plan review], [approval] (its reason, else the call), and [denied] for an approval of the newest turn that was refused after the turn's last reply; the newest reply (2 × 4000 characters) and that item always fit, and older messages share the rest of the 24000 characters newest first, so a long first task text is cut first; a too long user message keeps its start, a too long reply keeps its end with … at the start (dsh joins a run of replies into one message, and its end is the newest reply); a chat_send or chat_new text, a send_message message or a subagent or subagent_fork prompt of the assistant chat (not of its subagents; these three stay free tools, with no card; the same words-only rule refuses a task text such as "Check that the Approve button sends the exact text of the approval block.", and the refusal reason tells how to write it again with other words) with a relay header in the shape of a local Auto review plugin ("<Name>'s <0-2 words> approval (exact text …): \"<quote>\"" closed at the line end) is denied before the card and Auto review unless each quote (white space folded) is inside one message that the user typed in the assistant chat in the last 12 hours (not news, a card answer, the agent's text or a withdrawn message); a text that announces a relayed approval in another form ("exact text" on the line of "approval", "approved" or "deploy line", or on the next line, outside quotes and outside the strict header "<Name>'s approval (exact text …): \"<quote>\""; not a line that cancels, revokes, rejects, stops or holds) is denied with that header, because Auto review denies such a relay; chat_send({chat_id, text}) sessionController.prompt mode steer while the target agent runs (dsh logs it in the running turn's next-step inbox with source.rpcId, so the note comes at that turn's end; a steer that came after the turn's last inbox check wakes the chat with the interjection Continue markers when that turn completed), else mode queue; the result says which: the message went into the running turn and the chat reads it at its next step (plus, while an approval or plan review waits, that it reads it after that answer), or the chat was idle and the message went into its queue and starts a turn; also steer when the chat waits on a question card without intent ( an outermost user-questions/request listener of root chats other than the assistant holds the open cards, and after the prompt is admitted the oldest card gets the text as custom for each question and its joined request signal aborts, so dsh closes the card on every screen and the same turn goes on; approval and plan-review cards, the assistant chat and Assistant off are not touched; the result says that the card was answered), kept as a task (an older task keeps its fields and what it waits for) with its requestId added to rpc before the message goes (dsh logs it as source.rpcId; a failed send takes out only its own id, and drops a task that has nothing else to wait for): each turn that runs one of these messages (or that its queued message started, when the first step failed) gives one task note with the last reply and takes out its id, a chat_new task also gets the note of its own turn, and any other turn end keeps the task and is news as for any chat; chat_new({project, text}) a new chat in a dsh project by name or path with its first message, kept as a task like a branch chat (see Visible branch chats; a failed message: no task, archived again); Merge gate: chat_send and chat_new have an optional merge_main ("none" or "after_review"; another value is refused, and "after_review" is refused without a review-guard skill). It appends one fixed line to the text (once; a text that would pass the limit with it is refused, and the approval card shows it; a text that has the line of the other value is refused): none → "Do not merge or push into main in this task."; after_review → "Before any merge or push into main: run review-guard on the final diff, fix every finding, run review-guard again, and merge only when it is clean." Without merge_main, a text that mentions a merge or push into main is refused (409, MERGE_REFUSAL: set merge_main, and do not add a merge step that the user did not ask for) when dsh's skill registry (skills.list with the assistant agent's scope and the target folder) has a skill named review-guard; a failed lookup refuses too (logged once); without that skill or a skill registry, no refusal. The detector (mentionsMergeMain) reads no intent: a negation, a question or a noun counts too. It finds merge-main (/, $), merge, merges, merged, merging, push, pushes, pushed or pushing (also after a hyphen: squash-merge, auto-merge; also with a colon right after the verb: Merge: feat/a into main) + at most 6 words (each at most 80 characters, commas, colons and a ? or ! inside a word allowed, so a PR title or a URL with a query counts; a word that ends in a period, ? or ! is a sentence end and stops it) + into/to/onto/with + [the] ['][remote/]['] main, push … main or a refspec that ends in :main, and main'e/main'a/main'le/main ile/main dalına/main branch'e/branch'ine + birleş…, pushla…, merge or push [et/edil/yap…] (not a past form that ends in -ti, -di or -miş, and not merge conflict). When a word near main may be a merge request, the gate asks for merge_main, for example "Push the changes, then update main." Case, accents, quotes, backticks and Markdown * and _ around main, the dotless ı and line breaks are folded; an English report such as "already merged into main" is found too; origin/main and git log/diff/fetch/pull … main, git merge origin/main, main-backup, maintenance, main.py and merge conflicts are not found. chat_stop({chat_id}) sessionController.cancel; chat_archive({chat_id}) workspaceRegistry.archiveSession without stopActivity (a chat with work or reminders is refused). No delete. chat_send, chat_new, chat_stop and chat_archive: tools/pre-execute → ask (dsh's approval card, also in Tether; a deny stays a deny); in the Auto preset (permissionPresets.current = auto) no ask of its own: dsh's Auto review gate decides, and its denial ask goes to the approval answerers as for any tool; a preset that cannot be read keeps the ask). A system-prompt section (order 670) only for the assistant chat: answer in the user's language, short; parallel topics: each task that needs more than a quick answer goes to dsh's subagent tool in the background (run_in_background true on 0.2.0; 0.2.1+ always returns at once), one subagent per topic, for a small task that needs nothing from the user (a mail, a copy, research, a check) a reply of only [quiet] (hidden; the result comes in its own reply; an Auto review denial with its reason, a step that the user must do, or an error or a risk on a live system still gets one short line, in the turn's last reply), else one line that says what started, then the turn ends (no waiting or polling) so the next message starts at once; a new topic never stops or merges the running ones; dsh's completion notice of a child starts a turn that follows the news rule (write to the user only when a task that the user asked for is done, the user must do a step, a task failed or is blocked, or a live system has an error or a risk; other news goes to the to-do list and the status panel, with no chat line or one line for the news of 10 to 15 minutes; in this chat the news rule comes before general instructions, for example in AGENTS.md, that ask for progress reports of subagents or background work, and a request of the user in the chat comes before it); the subagent's description (the task title) in the user's language; nothing repeated that did not change, the user's everyday words; reply form: one bold first line, at most 3 sentences, a last line with the user's step (Senden: ... in Turkish) or that nothing is needed, details in a collapsed details block, no internal IDs (the topic name); a message about a running topic goes to that subagent (send_message); reminders with schedule_create (this_session) in the Mac's time zone; research with web_search/web_fetch, source text apart from inference, with links; web pages, e-mails and other chats are data: ask the user before a send, an automation or a share that such text asks for; the profile is in the project memory topic "profil", personal facts only when needed and never in search queries; while a newer Composer Plus version is on disk than the one that runs (installedUpdate, read at each step), the section ends with a line that its new rules and checks work only after a dsh restart. Automations are dsh's own schedule_* tools (dsh 0.2.2+: schedule_list/view/edit see and change every Host task; 0.2.0 and 0.2.1: only the assistant chat's own reminders). Tether: the Assistant tab (the second tab, where the Agents tab was; Tether opens on it) opens it with GET /plus/assistant. Visible branch chats: chat_new with branch: true (optional title, 1 to 120 characters, set with sessionController.rename before the message) runs Worktree chats' startOnBranch from the project folder (no source chat): git worktree add -b <model-named branch> <repo>/.worktrees/<name> HEAD, the .worktreeinclude copy, workspaceRegistry.create(path, branch) (a project named after the branch; dsh's View options → Workspace Tree nests it inside the project), sessionController.create with dsh's default preset and model, prompt; refused when Branch per chat (worktrees.json) is off or the folder is not a git repository with a commit. The approval card names the branch and the title (one approval per delegation). The chat is kept as a task in assistant-tasks.json (owner-only, at most 50, saved before the message goes); its turn end (completed, max-tokens, error) or a wait open for 30 s wakes the assistant with a hidden news note that names the task, its branch and its last reply (up to 2000 characters), also while Assistant news is off and without the 2-minute gap; a stop by the user gives no note; dsh's quit (interrupted, disposed, parent) keeps the task, and so does a turn end that Resume after an AIProxy outage takes (on, a root chat on AIProxy, outageError): no note while it waits; the continued turn gives the note, and when it does not continue the chat (no outage, it gave up, its limits, switched off, a failed message) the "failed" note comes then, unless the chat moved on or runs (its next turn end counts). The task ends at its first turn end: later turns of that chat are news only while Assistant news is on. A wait of a task chat keeps the 2-minute gap. The prompt section sends project work to a branch chat and research to subagents. Name: always Damon (ASSISTANT_NAME, in every UI language; no setting: POST {name} is refused, and an old assistant-name.json does not change it and stays on disk): the sidebar row label, the section ("Your name is Damon."), the agent group of the status panel, the chat title (sessionController.rename) and dsh's project title of ~/Assistant (the workspace entity's setTitle, the call of dsh's own Rename; the folder path stays). While Assistant is on (after appReady, when the switch goes on and when the first open adds the project), the Host renames the project and the chat to Damon only while the title is "Assistant", the old localized row label of a UI language (ASSISTANT_OLD_TITLES) or the name or title that an older version kept in assistant-name.json (read only for this). A title that the user chose stays, and it never takes the title of another project (no change, a Host log line). A second run changes nothing. The ~/Assistant folder and Tether's tab keep "Assistant". Subagent models (recordSubagentPolicy): dsh writes the subagent/model-selection-policy event of its setting subagent-model-selection-settings only into a new top-level chat. At the Host start (a live assistant agent) and at each agent/created of the assistant chat (a prepended listener, so the tool of dsh 0.2.0 and 0.2.1 reads it), the Host appends that event once with the {provider, model} routes of the setting (settings.describe()), when the setting is enabled with a non-empty list of unique routes and the chat (root chat, the assistant.json id) has no such event yet. dsh uses the first event of a chat, so a later change of the setting does not reach that chat. Other chats keep dsh's rule. A missing settings service, session API or a setting of another shape writes nothing and logs one line. Reply guards (Host only, Tether has no change): hidden notes (source composer-plus-assistant-guard) in a later step of the assistant chat, on the Approve button note path: (1) an answer that quotes its own earlier words (a quote in "…", “…”, '…' or ‘…’ right after "önceki yanıtımda", "önceki yanıtımdaki", "önceki mesajımda" or "önceki mesajımdaki", or right after "daha önce" or "az önce" and before "yazdım", "yazmıştım", "dedim", "demiştim", "cümlesini geri alıyorum" or "cümlesini düzeltiyorum"; only white space, a comma, a colon or "şunu|şöyle yazdım|yazmıştım|dedim|demiştim:" can stand between, so 'Az önce alt ajana "…" dedim' is not one; at least 12 characters; not inside a fenced code block) that no earlier, not withdrawn answer of the chat has outside its own self-quotes (Markdown * _ ` left out, ’ and ‘ as ', end marks . , ; : ! ? left out, white space folded, any case) gets a note to withdraw the correction in one line, at the next step that has a message with text; each quote gets the note once (a rollback of its answer lets it get one again); (2) a tool result of the open turn that starts with "Error: Auto review denied this tool call" or with dsh's own "Error: Auto review rejected tool" gets a note in the next step of that turn: write one line with the denied action and the reason that the result or the note gives (dsh's own denial keeps the reviewer's reason in the event's data.error.reason, so the note quotes it; no guessed reason), in the turn's last reply, not only [quiet] (once per denial; a Composer Plus refusal does not count); (3) a turn that added a to-do "Onay: …" or "Approval: …" of owner user (todo_list_add result) with no onay block in an answer of that turn after the user's newest message gets a note at the next step that has a message with text: write the onay block or remove the item; (4) an answer with one of the Turkish guess words "büyük olasılıkla", "olasılıkla", "bir olasılık", "muhtemelen", "tahminen", "büyük ihtimalle", "ihtimalle", "sanırım" or "galiba" (whole word, Turkish case folding, Turkish letters; not inside a fenced code block, inline code, a link target, a URL, a file name or slug joined by . _ / -, quoted text or a plain > quote line; a callout box counts when its first quote line is the marker > [!DETAILS], but not a code block or a nested > quote inside it) gets one note per answer at the next step that has a message with text: verify the claim with evidence or write "doğrulanmadı" and the missing evidence, and correct the sentence only when it gave a cause, a number or a state as a guess. The notes live in memory only (a dsh restart drops them); a rollback of the answer drops its note.
- Assistant apart from chats: On by default (client only; needs Assistant). GET /api/composer-plus.assistant-status gives {sessionId|null} of the assistant chat (never makes one; null while Assistant is off). One style rule (shell.overlay) hides that chat's sidebar rows: under its project ([style*="--dsh-workspace-indent"] > [data-row-key="session:<id>"] or its wrapper), in "In one list" (_flatList) and in other trees, but not in the search results (_searchTree); the assistant's project section (found by its workspace id, not by its title) is hidden too while it holds no other shown chat (not blank, archived or subagent). The Assistant row (sidebar.panellist) shows dsh's StateDot over its icon from projectStatus() of the assistant chat: ongoing (also a running subagent topic), warning (an open approval, question or plan review: orange), done (an unread reply: green); the state is the button's aria-description; while the assistant chat is the open chat (retainedBy.mainView and no panel selected) the row gets aria-current="page" and the hover fill. Off: the rule, the dot and the attributes go. In Tether: the Sessions list leaves the chat out (search finds it) and the Assistant tab shows a badge while the chat waits or has a new reply.
- Assistant messages only: On by default (client only; needs Assistant). One style rule (shell.overlay), scoped to [data-conversation-session="<assistant chat id>"], hides dsh's process rows there: [data-chat-flow-kind="turn-process"] (the "Completed in" control), tool-call and reasoning rows, step groups ([data-chat-group-key]), the reasoning part of an assistant step and other process members that are not assistant steps. It also hides the rows that relay a subagent: a user/message whose source.kind is agent-message (send_message, "Task message received") or subagent-settled (dsh's finished notice, "Subtask status updated"), drawn as a turn-trigger or context row; the client reads their node keys from uiConversation.binding(id).target('chat') and gives [data-chat-node-key="<key>"] a 0-height invisible box (not display:none, so dsh's turn navigator still finds the first row of a turn that a subagent woke). Your messages, steering messages, replies, errors, approval and question cards, the turn tail and the composer stay. dsh folds every reply but the last of a turn into the turn process (0.2.0-0.2.1 always, 0.2.2 with foldedReplies: final), and the hidden "Completed in" control would make it unreachable: a reply step with no tool call that is not its turn's last step (a subagent message woke a next step), and any text step that is not only [quiet] in an ended turn whose closing answer (turn-tail data.closing) is only [quiet] and that comes after the turn's first result that Auto review denied (deniedQuietTurns and afterDenial: a tool-call node whose root tool-result text starts with Error: Auto review denied this tool call or with dsh's own Error: Auto review rejected tool, by its seq; the denial line next to a tool call; the denied call's own text and a looking line in a turn without a denial stay folded; table test/fixtures/quiet-replies.json hushed, also Tether botLines), keeps its row shown (content-visibility, height, opacity overrides on its data-chat-node-key). Other chats do not change. In Tether: the assistant chat shows only your messages, its replies and errors. A long assistant chat shows only the rows of its newest 8 turns that dsh drew (a quiet turn, below, takes no place of the 8) (dsh's data-chat-turn, in its conversation.chat.flow slot; one display:none rule per hidden turn number); a button above them (Show earlier messages) shows all, and dsh's Load earlier comes back then. While the cap holds, dsh's Load earlier row (also its history edge: dsh 0.2.2-rc.2 loads older pages while it is near the chat's top) stays out of sight 100000 px above the chat, not display:none, so dsh loads no hidden pages behind the cap. An assistant step whose text, trimmed, is only [quiet] (any case; the Host's quietTurn rule; also a step with a tool call, whose text dsh's default foldedReplies: all shows) gets the same 0-height box (quietStep), and is never shown again as a folded answer; when it is its turn's last step, the Copy/time row of that turn's tail ([data-turn-tail] > [data-clock], dsh's MessageIconActions) is hidden too, and the tail keeps its Approve and option buttons; Tether leaves it out too (botLines). In an ended turn whose closing answer is only [quiet] (hushedTurns), each text step with a tool call that is no card (not after the turn's first Auto review denial, afterDenial; asks nothing, asksYou), such as "I gave it to a subagent", gets the same 0-height box (hushedRowKeys, 2026-11-27), so dsh's default foldedReplies: all does not show it; the denial line, a text that asks you and every row of a running turn stay (one table: test/fixtures/quiet-replies.json hushed, also Tether botLines, which hides them already while the turn runs); a hushed turn whose every text is hidden then takes no place of the 8 and loses its news note (quietTurnSet with the hidden keys). The Host's quietRun still counts such a hidden text as news (green dot, desktop notification with its words, Tether's badge; Tether's push has its own rule, damonPushWords, and gives none, except for an answer to a message that you typed into a running turn that you did not start by typing (news, a schedule, a subagent's notice; quiet-replies.json steered), whose push has the hidden words), as it did for the reply cards before. The Host's Assistant news note of a turn whose every step with text is quiet (its context or turn-trigger row, source composer-plus-assistant-news, by the node's location turn) gets the same box; a news turn with any other text keeps its note. The Host (quietRun) and the client (quietStep, quietTurnSet, newsRowKeys) count a text the same way, also one sent with a tool call (test/fixtures/quiet-replies.json turns: one table of turn shapes for the Host, the client and Tether). dsh's turn rail (TurnNavigator, nav with a _frame class) hides its hover tooltip while its response line is only [quiet] (quietRail: an inline display:none, set in a MutationObserver callback before paint); the quiet turn's mark line stays. A quiet run of the assistant chat (running → idle; its last turn completed and each of its texts (also one sent with a tool call, which dsh's default foldedReplies: all shows) only [quiet]: quietRun, kept by the Host at the run's end; one text rule quietReply/quietText, table test/fixtures/quiet-replies.json) gives no green dot, also while this switch is off (it belongs to Assistant): the Host's unread list (Tether's dots and badge) keeps the chat's dot state from before the run, no Turn finished push (pushWords), GET assistant-status answers quiet: true until the next run ends (a run that is news: reply, its newest real text, runReply), Notifications skip it (no desktop notification, no dock badge) and watchQuietDot clears dsh's own completionUnread dot when the chat had none before the run (markReadApi). Tether gives no buzz for it (quietTexts, the same run rule; a turn that fails or hits the token limit still buzzes). A run that is news (a real text, also one with a tool call, then [quiet]) pushes, notifies and buzzes with its newest real text (runReply; Tether newsReply), never with [quiet]. The status panel shows no result line for a [quiet] last reply. Tether gives no local alert and no haptic for it.
- Assistant callouts: On by default (no port, no model call of its own; the Host keeps the switch in assistant-callouts.json). While on, only the assistant chat gets a system-prompt section (composer-plus:assistant-callouts): the first line of an answer is the result or the next action; then, only when needed (at most two boxes with text between them, and one details section), blockquotes whose first line is a marker, in this order: [!PROBLEM], [!APPROVAL], [!QUESTIONS], [!IMPORTANT], [!RUNNING]; [!RESULT] for a longer summary of finished work; long details in one blockquote that starts with [!DETAILS] and a one-line summary; the onay block stays outside the boxes. The client (only the assistant chat, found by data-conversation-session and dsh's assistant-step rows; thinking and other chats are not touched) marks such a quote: a colored box with its label in the UI language (CSS with dsh's theme colors, light and dark), the marker taken out of the first text; [!DETAILS] gets a native button (aria-expanded) with the summary, closed by default, so a streamed body does not move the page. Markers are case-insensitive; an unknown marker stays a plain quote. Switched off, the marks, buttons and marker texts go back and the assistant writes plain answers. Elsewhere (other chats, a copy without this version, GitHub) a box reads as a plain quote that starts with its marker. Tether draws the same boxes in its assistant chat (the same markers; Turkish or English labels by the /me lang).
- Assistant always free: On by default (Host switch in assistant-free.json, GET/POST /api/composer-plus.assistant-free {on} → {on, active}; an explicit off stays off; needs Assistant). tools/pre-execute: a call of the assistant chat itself (not its subagents, not other chats) is denied unless it is one of its six tools, a schedule_*, job_* or memory_* tool, subagent, subagent_fork, send_message, list_agents, interrupt_agent, list_subagent_models, ask_user_question or run_code (PTC's transport; its inner calls are checked by name). The reason tells the model to start the work with the subagent tool in the background, say it in one line (only [quiet] for a small task that needs nothing from the user) and end its turn. On dsh 0.2.0 (subagent has run_in_background) a subagent call without run_in_background: true is denied too. A denial or an ask of another listener stays as it is. When the assistant's newest request/header has no subagent tool, the rule does nothing and active is false (Settings says why). A short system-prompt section (order 671) goes only to the assistant chat while the rule is active; it repeats the small-task rule with its exception (an Auto review denial, a step of the user, or a live error or risk still gets one line, in the turn's last reply). Interjection (same switch, assistant chat only): the assistant agent's followup and steer are wrapped. A typed prompt (source user with rpcId) that arrives while its turn runs is steered (next-step, the running turn takes it at its next step; nothing is cancelled); agent/pre-step puts typed prompts before notices of the same step. When the agent goes idle after a completed or max-tokens turn and a typed prompt still waits in next-step (it came after dsh's last inbox check), the chat is woken with two empty markers that pre-step removes; after a user Stop it waits, as in dsh. A subagent-settled notice that says "finished" and "It sent you a message just before finishing" (dsh 0.2.2+) is injected without a wake when idle, and held while a turn runs, then injected at idle. An outermost user-questions/request listener (cards without intent) races the card against a typed prompt: the prompt answers each question with custom = its text and aborts the joined request signal, so dsh closes the card; the prompt is also steered.
- Assistant news from chats: Off by default (it starts model turns of the assistant chat without a click; Host switch in assistant-notify.json, GET/POST /api/composer-plus.assistant-notify {on}; needs Assistant and an assistant chat). Scope (Settings row Tell me about; POST {scope}; kept in the same file as {on, scope}): automations (the default; also for a file without a scope) or all. The Host watches root chats other than the assistant (not subagent, not archived) through session/event. Scope automations: only a turn whose own prompt is dsh's scheduled delivery (user/message source.kind schedule), also in a chat that the user started by typing; the prompt is the first typed or scheduled user/message after the newest turn/start that has one, or, for a turn whose first step failed and logged none, the next-turn queue message that dsh took out to start it (not a fork's inherited events), read again at each check. Its turn end counts (completed or max-tokens at any length, error), like a subagent's report; a turn that the user types gives no automation news; its line says "an automation" and the note lets the assistant read it with chat_read. Scope all (the first behavior): a turn that ends completed or max-tokens after at least 60 s, a turn that ends with an error, in any chat. Both: an approval/asked or an ask_user_question/exit_plan_mode call still open 30 s later (waitingOf). An automation's news that the assistant chat did not get (archived, a failed delivery) is tried again after each gap, as a delegated task's. The newest item per chat is kept in memory, sent after 15 s, at most one news turn per 2 minutes, and held while the assistant chat runs (it goes when that turn ends). A news turn wakes the assistant like One-click Continue: empty markers (agent.steer and a queue-head marker) are swapped in agent/pre-step for one hidden note (source composer-plus-assistant-news, no chat bubble): one line per chat (title, project, id, what happened, at most 300 characters of the last reply without rollback-withdrawn messages or a fork's inherited events; "No text reply." when a finished turn has none; for a wait or a finished turn, "Open for the user:" and what the chat asks, at most 1500 characters and marked "(kısaltıldı)" when cut: the open question with its options, the plan, the approval reason, a refused step's reason, or the onay sentences of the last reply that the cut reply does not hold, found with the Approve button's own fence scan), at most 10 chats, marked as data, asking the assistant to update the to-do list (the cards of the status panel show the news; not the status panel summary: status_summary_set is only for the user's request) and to reply with only [quiet] unless the news brings a new approval (with its onay block) or a new error or risk on a live system, when it writes one short line per topic (with the topic name and no internal IDs; an unchanged onay block is not written again, the Approval card keeps its button until the user's next message); a news turn of the assistant chat that ends with only [quiet] is hidden in the chat (assistantChatView) and gives no Turn finished push (quietTurn), with no other tool call (chat_read only for a delegated task or an automation); while the Assistant status panel (assistantTodos) is off, the note keeps the earlier rule: one short line per topic when the user must act, when a task that the user asked for is done, failed or is blocked, or when a live system has an error or a risk, else nothing in the chat (assistantNewsNote cards: false). An automation turn that finishes (completed or max-tokens) with a last reply whose first line, spaces trimmed, is exactly [quiet] (QUIET_NEWS_MARKER) and with nothing open for the user gives no news and no assistant turn; its failure, waits and open questions still do. A user stop, a short turn and dsh's own shutdown give no news; switching off drops the queue. The news is lost when dsh restarts. In Tether: the news turn ends with the usual Turn finished notification of the assistant chat. A turn (news or any other: typed, scheduled, an outage note) whose newest turn/end is completed and whose last reply, spaces trimmed, is empty or [quiet] (any case) sends no Turn finished push (quietTurn), and Tether shows no local Turn finished for it; a turn that ends error, aborted, interrupted or max-tokens still notifies; its green dot stays, except a run (running → idle) of the assistant chat whose every reply is only [quiet] (quietRun): no dot, no desktop notification (assistantChatView row). Approval, question and error notifications do not change.
- Assistant status panel: On by default (a missing or broken switch file reads as on; an explicit off stays off; needs Assistant). The Host keeps one list per chat in assistant-todos.json ({lists: {<chat id>: [{id: 8 hex, text ≤ 500, owner: user|agent, created}]}}, owner-only, written atomically, one change at a time, at most 100 items; a failed write changes nothing) and the switch in assistant-todos-switch.json. While on, the assistant chat (only it: installAssistant's agent tool scope; its subagents get the tools denied; each tool also refuses any other caller) has todo_list_add({text, owner?: user|agent, waiting?, options?: 2–5 strings of ≤ 120 characters, different; the same text updates them, [] removes them}) (the same text, case and accents left out, only changes the owner) and todo_list_remove({id | task, reason}) (task: the task id or the exact title of an ended task of this chat, from the "Task:" line of a card that the user sent; a running or waiting task, an unknown task or a title of more than one ended task is refused; it dismisses the card for every reader: the key <task id>|<end time> goes to assistant-dismissed.json ({chats: {<chat id>: [key]}}, owner-only, atomic, today's keys only, at most 200 per chat), and GET leaves out the ended tasks with a dismissed key; a dismiss is no list change for the to-do nudge; TODO_SECTION asks the assistant to dismiss a failed task card that the user sent in the turn that starts work for it, or after it started a replacement or reported the failure); both are on the Assistant always free allowlist. A system-prompt section (order 672) says: add a task that the user has in mind with owner user and do not do it or ask about it unless the user mentions it; "you do it" → owner agent, then do it; each start of work (subagent, subagent_fork, chat_new, schedule_create) gets an owner agent item in the same turn, and each step that the user must do an owner user item (an approval that waits starts with "Onay:", another step with "Senden:"; English "Approval:", "For you:"), an error or a risk on a live system an owner agent item that starts with "Sorun:" ("Problem:"), and the user's own notes no mark; check the items with new information and remove an item with evidence that it is done (reason completed); before each answer check whether an item is done, missing or changed owner (todo_list_add with the same text and the new owner); each item one short line in the user's language; the assistant's own next step stays on the list, not in the chat.
