A runtime context (order 650, interpolate false, only the assistant chat, empty for an empty list; `{{` broken up) gives the current items (id, owner, JSON text) marked as data; it changes only when the list changes, so the prompt cache holds; during a turn the context keeps the list of the turn start when the assistant changes it with its own tools (their results tell the change), so dsh sends one copy of the runtime context per turn, and the panel's remove or a compaction shows the current list at the next step. To-do nudge: when an assistant turn ends that called subagent, subagent_fork, chat_new or schedule_create and neither todo_list_add nor todo_list_remove, the same runtime context also has one line that asks for the item (TODO_NUDGE); a list change or the next turn end takes it away; the Host writes no item itself. Client: a dock entry (conversation.input.dock, order 2) only in the assistant chat (assistant-status) publishes dsh's [data-conversation-content] chat body, and the panel is portaled into it. Place `side` (default): a 300 px column at the top right of the chat body, the chat gets 332 px right padding while the panel is at the right, also while it is folded (the folded panel still shows its header and the Onay card), max-height is the chat body height minus 180 px, scrolls inside; it is not dsh's right sidebar. Place `top`: the first flex item of the chat body (order -1, as wide as the chat column, max-height 40vh, scrolls inside). A place button in the panel header, next to Refresh, switches the place; its aria-label and title name the place where it moves the panel (status.placeTop "Show above the chat" while at the right, status.placeSide "Show at the right of the chat" while above). The choice is in localStorage `dsh-composer-plus.status-place` (`side` or `top`). In a window narrower than 1000 px the panel always shows above the chat and the place button hides. The cards and the summary card are flat: no background of their own, and a thin colored line at the left only on the active item; the panel is the only box. The header buttons Get summary, Projects, Refresh and the place button are icon buttons: each keeps its label as aria-label and tooltip, and Get summary shows a spinner while it waits. A delegated chat that is archived (workspaceRegistry.archivedSessionIds, also by chat_archive) shows no task card, open or ended; unarchived, it shows again. Projects leaves out the assistant chat, archived chats and chats that a scheduled task opened (an automation: its first turn's prompt is a schedule delivery). The panel is a card stack (the Damon card stack; statusCards in client.js groups the answer, one table: test/fixtures/status-cards.json). The panel reads GET /api/composer-plus.assistant-todos?sessionId= on open, at each turn end, every 5 s while the chat runs (not in a hidden tab) and after each action (the newest read wins; one action per chat at a time). The own notes of the user (items of owner user without a mark) are one Kararlar button at the bottom (decide.title; Furkan 2026-11-24): a badge counts the open decisions (isDecision: an item with options, or a text that starts with "Karar ver"/"Decide" or has "karar ver:"), a count the other notes, decide.none when none waits. A click opens DecisionDialog, a native <dialog> opened with showModal() and portaled into document.body (top layer, the page inert, ::backdrop dimmed with backdrop-filter blur; role dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby; Esc (cancel and close events), × and a backdrop click close it; the focus goes back to the button). One decision card at a time (list order, Sonra ids at the end): a header with the counter "i / N" between two buttons (data-dc-nav="prev" and "next", ‹ and ›, aria-label decide.prev and decide.next) that go to the previous or the next card without an answer; the text, decide.added, one button per option (decisionOption: the recommended word in parentheses becomes a tag; the recommended option is preselected and marked), Atla (skip, this opening only), Sonra (to the end, this page), Sil (decide.remove, as on a note row below), a decide.other field with decide.send. A click on an option, or the key 1–9, sends decide.message ("Karar: <item> → <option>") at once through Option picks' send path (createOptionPicks.say: conversation.send, one send per chat at a time; quick clicks wait in order; a click within 400 ms of the last action does nothing) and shows the next card at once; after the send resolves (dsh took the message: while the assistant works it waits in dsh's queue or goes into the running turn, so no answer is lost), a status line decide.sent ("✓ Sent: <answer>", role status) confirms it. The Send button is never disabled: it sends the typed text of the field when the field has text, else the recommended option (its label decide.sendWhat, "Send: <answer>"), else it puts the focus in the field; Enter does the same with the namesLive rule (Enter does not send an option that names a live system: the user clicks it). The text of the field is a draft per card (per item id): it goes only with the decision on screen, so a card that comes back later cannot take the text typed for another card. The item stays on the list (the assistant removes it, TODO_SECTION); the panel hides an answered id (panel state `answered`: item ids, kept per chat with the per-card `drafts` in a module map (decideKept) while the panel draws again, for the life of the page; there is no DECIDE_HIDE_MS any more) until the item leaves the list; a reload of the page shows an item that the assistant did not remove; a failed send drops the id, so the card comes back with its draft and decide.failed (kept in the panel state, so the panel shows it under the button after the dialog closed); a click while another send of the chat runs (Onayla, an option button) waits for it. Keys in the dialog (after 800 ms, not in the field; the dialog stops their propagation): 1–9 send that option (not an option that names a live system), ArrowLeft and ArrowRight go to the previous and the next card; Enter sends like the Send button. After the decisions: the other notes with Yaptım (decide.noteMessage "Not tamam: <item>"), Atla and Sil (decide.remove: the panel's remove action at once, no message, no confirmation; aria-disabled while another change of the list runs; a failure brings the row back and shows todos.failed); then decide.allDone and Kapat. The focus stays in the dialog (the question, the notes title or the end line) when a card or a row goes; closed, it goes back to the button or, when the button is gone, to the panel title. A backdrop click closes the dialog only when the pointer went down on the backdrop too. Auto-open (DecidePeek, canPeek): when a decision id that this page has not seen appears, the dialog opens by itself once for it, only while the chat body is visible, document.visibilityState is visible, the composer is empty (no text, no attachment), no other dialog, menu or listbox is open, and no keydown happened in the last 3000 ms. It opens non-modal with the `open` attribute and `data-peek` (not show()/showModal(), which move the focus; the page is not inert, no ::backdrop), so what the user types stays in the composer; the modal checks of other features (KeepFocus, Find in chat, keys 1–9 on a question card, the canvas Esc, busyNow) use `dialog[open]:not([data-peek])`. A click on the Kararlar button while a peek is open switches it to modal (close(), showModal()). Esc closes a peek from anywhere (a document capture listener with preventDefault, so it is no half of dsh's Esc Esc stop) unless another dialog or menu is on screen; closing it from inside gives the focus to the composer. Decision ids on the list at the panel's first good read on this page count as seen, and ids shown in an open dialog count as seen; after the user closes it (Esc, ×, Close) it opens again only for a newer decision id. The panel has no → or × of a note any more (Sil and Yaptım in the dialog do their work). Get suggestions: the row (suggest.row, with suggest.rowHint; suggest.again once cards exist) sits under the card area of DecisionDialog, also at the end view (decide.allDone). A click calls the panel store's askSuggest (POST {sessionId, action: "suggest"}); one request per chat at a time. The Host sends a hidden note (source kind composer-plus-status-suggest as the marker; the logged note keeps the summary note's source kind composer-plus-status-summary, so DAMON_PROMPTS and Tether's damonPrompts treat it as a hidden note). The note asks the assistant to collect the chat and memory_recall, start one background subagent that reads the project notes only in subfolders of its folder (never the folder root, never a folder named Gizli, read only) (an instruction to the model, not a guard; Protected files is no hard rule either: protectedHit checks only the path argument of dsh's file tools read, read_image, grep, write, edit and str_replace_editor, not a shell command, a glob or a grep over a folder), then call status_suggestions_set and reply only [quiet], with no to-do item: the first subagent call after the note does not count as work for the to-do nudge (another work tool in that turn still does). status_suggestions_set({suggestions: [{project?, title, text, why, source, unverified?}]}) works only in the assistant chat (1 to 8 items; title ≤ 120, text ≤ 600, why ≤ 300, source ≤ 200, project ≤ 120 characters). It cleans each item (todoText, the limits) and drops an item whose raw or cleaned field matches the approval/decision rule (suggestBlocked: after folding (look-alike letters of both cases (Latin small capitals and IPA, Greek, Cyrillic, Armenian, Cherokee, Lisu, Coptic) and colon look-alikes to ASCII by Unicode confusables.txt, before and after NFKD; marks, format, default-ignorable and control characters removed; Turkish lower case; ı and l read as i; accents go, so Decisión: and Décision : count too) the approval forms that Auto review accepts (onaylı, onaylıdır, onaylıyorum, onaylıyoruz, onayladım, onay veriyorum/verdim, izin veriyorum/verdim, I approve, approved:), karar: or decision: anywhere, the strict line canlı deploy <product> <sha>; a text or line that starts (after spaces or tabs) with CANLI DEPLOY in capitals (each look-alike reads as a capital, I i l L read as one letter, and the two words may touch); look-alikes outside the pair list (another script, a digit or sign such as 1 or |) are not caught; a word (a run of Latin, Greek and Cyrillic letters) with 3 or more Latin letters and a Cyrillic or Greek letter, so a unit such as µs or kΩ and Japanese or Chinese text with β版 pass), and it refuses when none is left. It keeps the newest set per chat in memory (ponytail: gone after a dsh restart). GET gives suggest {at, items}, suggestAsked (the request time) and suggestMissed (the request is open for 15 minutes; missed when the turn that took the note ended with no subagent call and without the tool). While it waits, the dialog shows suggest.loading; it shows suggest.late (missed, forgotten or 15 minutes) or suggest.failed, then the cards (cp-dc-sg: optional project tag, title, text, suggest.why, suggest.source, and the suggest.unverified tag). A click on a card sends suggest.message ("Öneri: <title> — <text>" in Turkish) through createOptionPicks.say in the dialog's send chain, once per card (decide state `suggested`, kept per chat for the page; the card then shows suggest.sent), and the client checks the same rule again before a send (suggestionMessage returns null). The Kararlar button always shows (data-decide-none on it when nothing waits). Tether has no Kararlar dialog, so it has no row; it ignores the new GET fields. Each project row has → too (aria-label status.insert "Write in the message box: <name>", title status.insertShort). The card buttons are icons, at most two: → is the main step: cards.ask (Sorun), cards.reply or cards.done (Senden: "cards.doneMessage" with the title), statusInsert for a Running item without a task; × removes an item at once (no confirmation), hides a failed task's Problem card or hides a Done today card (cards.seen "Seen" is its label); the other actions are under "…" (aria-label cards.more "More actions: <item>"): cards.open (Open the chat), status.insertShort, todos.handoverShort, queue.later, todos.removeShort. A click on a task card opens the task's chat (the title stays a button for the keyboard). There is no Watch button and no Details disclosure. These actions write into the composer: statusInsert writes the row's data the same way (insertText at the end, on a new line after a draft, focus; nothing sent), one field per line in the UI language without ids: an item: status.insert.item, status.insert.owner (Damon) and, when it waits, status.insert.state (todos.waiting · time · todos.overdue) and status.insert.reason; a task: status.insert.task (left out when the title is the chat id), status.insert.state (state · time), status.insert.result, status.outageRow; a project: status.insert.project and status.insert.summary or status.projectChats. A long title wraps instead of running under the buttons. Cards: the Host's answer becomes one card per topic (statusCards): an item and a task with the same text (case and accents left out, after the mark) are one card, and the more urgent state wins (an error, then a wait, then the task's state). The mark at the start of an item's text decides the group: "Onay:" (English "Approval:") the Approval card's items, "Sorun:" ("Problem:") the Problem card, "Senden:" ("For you:") the For you card; a failed task is a Problem card, a waiting task or an item that waits for the user a For you card, a running task or another item of owner agent a Running card, a task that ended today a Done today card; an item of owner user without a mark is one of the user's own notes. Order: the count bar (cards.count.onay/sorun/senden/suruyor/bitti, or cards.none; Get summary, Projects, Refresh and a fold button), the summary card, the Approval card (cards.onay; the sentences of the newest `onay` block that the chat offers, each with the Approve button (approve.button) that sends the exact sentence through Option picks' store, the same path and guard as the button under a reply; the items with the mark; a cards.live label when a sentence names a live target; only while the chat offers a sentence (an onay block with its button): without one, the items with the mark show no card, no count and no queue entry and stay on the list; the buttons show only while the composer is empty), then Problem, For you, Running and Done today (a group has its own fold button; Problem is always open; a group that does not fit among the first 3 cards starts folded; Done today starts folded and folding it marks its cards seen, cards.fresh/cards.new), and the Kararlar button (decide.title) with the user's own notes. The open panel is one list: there are no Cards / Queue / Briefing buttons and no Queue or Briefing view. A group that holds the active item opens unless the user folded it. The Done today header is one line with its count and the "new" count. Card lines are short: a For you card shows only the wait time (and Overdue after 24 h), a Running task only the time it runs, a Done today card the end time and the duration (the state word only for stopped or failed). The date (Briefing's old line) is the tooltip of the count bar. The count bar, the summary card and the Approval card stay in place while the cards scroll. A separator under the summary card (role separator, aria-orientation horizontal, aria-valuenow/min/max, tabIndex 0, focus ring; label status.resizeSummary, tooltip status.resizeSummaryHint) sets the card's max-height: a drag with the main mouse button (pointer capture; the card follows the pointer; saved at pointerup, a cancelled drag puts the old height back), Up/Down one line (18 px), a double-click the default (14vh); at least 92 px (the title and about 3 lines), at most the room of the panel (its max-height less the rest of the fixed part and up to 96 px of the cards; measured after each draw of the panel and on a window resize, with a hidden absolute probe that has the panel's max-height in the panel's parent; a drag and the keys use the last measured room). This browser keeps it (localStorage dsh-composer-plus.status-summary-height), so a chat switch and a reload keep it; a saved height that does not fit a smaller window shows at the room's size. The fixed part has no 40vh cap of its own: it takes the panel's height, and the cards shrink first and scroll. Tether has no such separator (its summary is a section of the Status sheet). × of a failed task's Problem card and × of a Done today card (cards.seen) POST {sessionId, action: "dismiss", task: "<task id>|<end time>"} (the Host list above, so every browser and Tether leave the card out) and hide the card in this browser at once (localStorage dsh-composer-plus.status-tasks-dismissed: <task id>|<end time>, kept as the fallback while the Host call fails, only today's keys stay; a new end of the same task shows it again; dsh-composer-plus.status-done-seen: when the Done today group was last folded); a Done today card goes when the day ends. With a card stack in the chat, the Approve button of the assistant chat is only in the Approval card and the onay sentence stays in the reply as gray text (ApproveButtons and OnayCodeBlocks read the stack through createCardOffers; other chats are unchanged; when dsh renames data-conversation-content the stack does not show and the button is under the reply again).  Status panel (same switch): GET ?sessionId=<assistant chat> also answers {tasks, projects, summary?, at} — tasks: the assistant's direct subagents from its own subagent/catalog events (a fork's copy and external executions left out; done before today left out; at most 20): {id, title (catalog label), state: running|waiting (open approval/question/plan review)|done|failed|stopped (turn/end reason), started, ended?, result? (first line of the last reply or the error, ≤ 160)}; a chat that the assistant starts or messages (chat_new, with or without branch, and chat_send; assistant-tasks.json) is also a task while its turn runs (chat: true, state running|waiting; a branch chat has result "<project> · <branch>"); after its turn ends, a live delegated chat stays an open task while one of its dsh background jobs runs (running) or while its last answer asks the user (an onay block, an open question, a refused step: waiting), also after the bot ended its task; the panel watches these chats' live state and reads the Host every 5 s while such a row runs; when the bot ends that task at its turn end and nothing of this holds, the chat stays a task until the day ends (chat: true, state done|failed|stopped, started, ended, result: first line of the last reply or the error, ≤ 160), after the open tasks, newest end first with the ended subagents (installAssistant's endedTasks Map: in memory only, so a dsh restart loses it; at most 50; while the same chat has a new task, its ended row does not show (a chat_send whose message did not go shows it again)); a task that the bot keeps (dsh's quit, an AIProxy outage; assistant-tasks.json, so also after a restart) is running or waiting only while its chat runs (or for 15 s after a new task, while its message goes; its time starts at the chat's newest turn), else failed (its last turn ended with an error: an AIProxy outage, 429, 500, 503 or 504) or stopped, with the time of the chat's last turn (its live log, else its saved log, read once until its next turn, else dsh's chat list time), today only; an ended row's time also starts at the chat's newest turn; projects: workspaces with root chats updated in the last 24 h (a chat below a project folder, such as a .worktrees branch folder, counts for it; no assistant, subagent, blank or archived chat; at most 5; 5 chats each; the chat list is kept 30 s or until another root chat starts or ends a turn, an archived chat leaves at the next read, Refresh sends &refresh=1); an ended task is read once and kept for the dsh run; summary: the last status_summary_set({projects: [{project, text}]}) (1–8 projects, assistant chat only, assistant-summary.json owner-only). GET ?sessionId=&project=<workspace id> answers {branch, commits: [{hash, at, subject}]} with read-only git (branch --show-current, log -5) in that registered folder only, 404 otherwise. The first line of STATUS_SECTION names the cards (Approval, Problem, For you, Running, Done today, the user's own notes) and asks the assistant to give an item and a task the same words; its news rule says: do not write news (a subagent result, a note about a chat, an automation, an interim report, a review round, a finished task) in the chat, update the to-do list (the cards change by themselves), then reply with only [quiet] (the chat hides that reply and it sends no notification), and write one line only for a new approval (with its onay block) or a new error or risk on a live system; this rule comes before the assistant section's News rule and before general instructions such as AGENTS.md. A line asks the assistant to call status_summary_set only for the Get summary note, a summary request in the chat or a scheduled task (the morning summary), and to write at most one sentence in the chat. StatusCanvas gets `islands` [{key, title, count, tone, body?, cards: [{key, label, el, side?, mine?, run?}]}] and `hub` {running, waiting}: the same card elements and handlers as the list (one data path), on a pan/zoom canvas that covers dsh's [data-conversation-content] chat body (position absolute, inset 0); the body gets data-composer-plus-canvas=open and its other children visibility:hidden (not unmounted: scroll and draft stay). Damon is a circle (the hub) in the middle with "N running" and "N wait for you". canvasLayout puts the islands at fixed places: the left column onay, senden, sorun at x −720; the right column suruyor, bitti, kararlar at x 320 (kararlar holds the Kararlar button, which opens the same decision dialog); updates (the reply cards of assistantReplyCards, only while that feature is on) above the hub at y −160 − h; ozet (the summary card and the projects, only when they show) below it at y 160; each island 400 px wide with a 48 px gap, the columns centered on the hub. A card cannot be dragged and no card place is saved. A line goes from the hub to each island, and a moving dashed line (.cp-cv-lines path.run; it stops with prefers-reduced-motion) to each card whose task runs now (`run`). canvasMode(k) decides what an island shows: far (k < 0.5) its title and count, near (0.5 ≤ k < 0.95) its cards, close (k ≥ 0.95) every line of a card. The view {x, y, k} moves by drag, Shift+wheel, a sideways wheel or trackpad swipe and the arrow keys; it zooms at the pointer by wheel, trackpad pinch, a two-finger touch pinch, the + and − buttons at the bottom left (with the percent) and the + and − keys, from 25% to 160%. 0 and the home button (data-cv-home, "Back to Damon") call canvasHome: the hub in the middle at 75%, smaller (at least 50%) when the two island columns do not fit 58 px from the sides (clear of the zoom buttons), 40% under 600 px. A click on an island's title zooms to that island. The minimap (data-cv-minimap, bottom right) shows the islands, a colored dot on an island that has something (mine), the hub and the visible part; a click moves the view, Enter or Space goes home. The "Only what waits for me" button (data-cv-only) shows only the cards with `mine` (senden, the approval, the choice, the unread reply cards) and dims the other islands (a dashed border and label-secondary text, no opacity: WCAG AA). A click or Enter on a card opens it in the side panel at the right (data-cv-side, the card's `side` element, so the buttons Approve, →, ×, "…" work as in the panel); there a click on a task card opens its chat. - Assistant reply cards: On by default (client only; needs Assistant): no Host route, no port, no model call; Tether shows each reply and failed turn of the Damon chat as a card too (replyHead: the same title and For you rule, test/fixtures/reply-titles.json), with its own read marks per Mac and Load earlier (markReplies, replyUnread, replyPage: one table, test/fixtures/reply-read.json; no 40 cap on the phone; tether/FEATURES.md). In the assistant chat, each reply is a card in the style of the Kararlar dialog cards, from dsh's chat nodes of the chat (uiConversation.binding(id).target('chat')). replyCardsOf(chat, withdrawn, inherited) gives the cards in seq order: a settled assistant-step with text and no tool call (unless it is the turn tail's closing answer, turn-tail data.closing.finalNode, or its text asks the user for something: an onay block, an option list or a Senden:/For you: line, which dsh 0.2.2 shows next to a tool call, or its ended turn's closing answer is only [quiet] and it comes after the turn's first result that Auto review denied: afterDenial), not quiet (quietText) and not in a quiet turn (quietTurnSet), and a turn-error node; a seq that a withdrawn span covers (Turn rollback and dsh-rewind-plugin: the Host's rollback route, rule 9) or that is below the inherited count of a fork (rule 10) is left out, and no card shows before the rollback route has answered. replySections(text) splits a reply at lines of only --- (3 or more hyphens, up to 3 spaces in, outside a ``` or ~~~ code block, so an onay block never splits) into trimmed parts without empty ones; each part is a card {key: <seq>:<i>, seq, last} with the reply's seq and time (the Approve offer keeps the reply's seq; each part has its own read id <seq>:<i>, so a click reads only that part, and a reply without --- keeps its seq as its read id; the option buttons show only on the last part; ASSISTANT_SECTION asks for one topic per card, an independent topic after a --- line with its own bold line, and no side topic that needs nothing from the user); replyParts(text) gives title (the bold first line, a heading, else the first sentence), forYou (a "Senden:" or "For you:" line, highlighted), body, details (a [!DETAILS] section, closed) and approvals (onayBlocks) and options (parseOptions). The newest reply that offers an onay block or an option list gets the Approve button and the option buttons, only while the message box is empty, on the send path of the buttons under a reply (optionPicks; one send per chat at a time); an older card shows the sentence and the options as text. A new card is unread (a blue left edge, the New label); the chat's feed shows the cards in seq order (the oldest on top, the newest at the bottom; it scrolls to the newest card when it opens and when a new card comes, and keeps the bottom while you are there; the card of the newest unread reply has a shadow), and replyOrder (unread first, each reply newest first, its parts in order) orders only the canvas's Updates island; in the feed and the canvas side panel the text of a card has the text cursor and can be selected, only buttons, links and the details summary have the hand, and a click that ends a text selection in the card does not read it; the status panel's chat toggle is an icon button in the header's icon row (a speech bubble line icon, struck through while the chat shows) with the label as aria-label and title; a click, Enter or a button of a card reads it, and Mark all as read reads all. The read store (localStorage dsh-composer-plus.reply-cards-read) keeps a floor and a list of read ids per chat (a seq, or <seq>:<i> for a part; an older seq mark reads every part of its reply; the floor moves over a split reply only when all its parts are read), merged on write (the higher floor, both lists), at most 50 chats and 200 read ids per chat; at the first view of a chat the older replies count as read (floor = the newest seq). ReplyFeed is drawn from shell.overlay (the overlay entry assistant-replies) into the chat body, over [data-conversation-scroll] (a measured box); the chat body gets data-composer-plus-replies="hidden" and the scroll body visibility:hidden, so the chat is hidden behind the cards by default (the composer stays as it is). Show the chat (in the status panel's top bar, or at the top of the cards when the panel is off) shows it, Hide the chat hides it again; localStorage dsh-composer-plus.assistant-chat-shown keeps the choice. A dock seat, assistant-reply-seat (conversation.input.dock, order 3), tells the status panel that the feature is on (replyFlag); the panel's canvas shows the same cards in its updates island. The feed shows the newest REPLY_MAX = 40 replies (all of their cards); older replies are in the chat. A Markdown image in a card (![alt](<absolute path>) as dsh asks agents to write it, or a path relative to the chat's folder) shows through dsh's own authenticated /api/file route, as in dsh's chat; only png, jpg, jpeg, webp and gif, else the alt text (also when the image does not load, in an option button, and in Tether). - Project memory: On for a new user: the first start of Composer Plus in a dsh home (no `<dsh home>/storages/dsh-composer-plus` folder yet) saves `memory.json` `{on: true}` at once, because Assistant keeps its notes there; an existing install keeps its setting (no file: off). While on, one model call after each finished turn. A memory per project folder (and a global one) in DS Bot's format: Agent Memory Repo Markdown (a main file `<project folder name> memory.md` (`hafıza` instead of `memory` while the UI language that a browser reported last is Turkish; `MEMORY.md` before 2026-11-12, still read) + topic files linked from `## Index`, one `- entry [source: …; added: …]` per line; no size limit; each main file gives its newest entries up to 8,000 characters to the prompt and counts the rest for `memory_recall`), under `$DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-composer-plus/memory/` (never in the project) or, with Settings → **Memory folder** (`memory-folder.json` `{folder}`, read at dsh start), only in that folder: `Genel/` (global) and `Projeler/<project folder name>/` (after Assistant setup's Set up, a new memory folder gets the UI language's names, saved as `names` in `memory-folder.json`; a folder that already has its subfolders keeps their names, nothing is renamed) with `project.json` `{path}` (the first start copies every old note there once, all or none; the memory stays off in a run where that copy failed), with `journal.jsonl` (every change) and `reviewed.json` (review cursor per chat). After each finished root turn, one call to the chat's own model reads the chat's own new messages (fork parent copy and rolled-back messages left out) and adds, edits or removes entries (also an entry that the messages show is done or out of date; the prompt section asks the agent to keep the memory current the same way); keys, passwords and ID numbers (also an 11-digit Turkish ID number with right check digits) are refused. Tools `memory_remember`, `memory_forget`, `memory_recall`; a subagent's tools and prompt use the project of its working directory (the folder of its task), a root chat's use its first folder; a folder in a git worktree (a `.git` file whose `commondir` names a `.git` folder, and that git's worktree list names) uses the memory of the main working tree (the same path below it), so a branch chat shares its repository's memory. At each start, before the memory is used, a migration (journal op `migrate`, every moved and dropped line) renames each main file and merges each memory whose project.json names a git worktree (or a gone `<repo>/.worktrees/<name>`) into its repository's memory: entries (an entry with the same text is left out; source and date stay), topics and Index links; the worktree's memory files go after every entry is read back. A folder whose repository is not found, or with lines written by hand, stays as it is. A note of the user's named `<x> memory.md` (not the folder's name, no `# Memory` title) is not a memory file and stays. A failed save puts its files back and keeps the memory off for that run. POST `{lang}` (the UI language) picks the word from the next start. The main files go into the system prompt, frozen per chat; a chat that dsh loads again (a dsh restart, a resumed subagent) keeps the notes of its newest logged prompt when that section's rule lines, project line and Topics lines are the same and each of its notes is still saved, so the prompt cache holds (only notes added since then are missing, as the section says; a removed or changed note, a new topic, a new chat and a fork get the current notes). Host switch `memory.json`. Settings → **Open memory**: every note by project (and global), a filter, and a text field: one call to dsh's default model (no tools, the notes are data) proposes add/edit/remove changes as a preview; only Apply writes them, all or none (a refused change saves nothing and shows the reason), only while the notes are unchanged since the preview (else 409), journal actor `editor`; one preview or apply at a time on the Host. Tether: chat title menu → Project memory (same route, `/plus/memory-edit`).
- Memory version history: On by default (Host switch `memory-history.json`); works while Project memory is on. Before each save of the memory (tool, review, Open memory's Apply, copy, accepted suggestion, restore), the Host keeps the memory files of each scope that the save changes, as they were, in `$DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-composer-plus/memory/history/<project id|global>/<ms>-<id>.json` (owner-only); the newest 50 per scope stay. A save that fails removes its copy; a copy that cannot be written stops the save (nothing is saved). Open memory → select one project or Global memory → **History**: versions newest first (date, who changed the memory after it, note count), a version's diff (what a restore changes, per file), **Restore**: all files of that version or none, only while the memory is unchanged since the diff opened (409), journal op `restore`; the memory before the restore is kept as a new version (a restore can be undone). One memory action at a time (409 busy). Tether: Project memory sheet → History (`/plus/memory-history`, no switch).
- Export memory to AGENTS.md: On by default (browser switch); works while Project memory is on. Open memory → select one project → **Export to AGENTS.md**: the Host builds a section of that project memory (main file notes, then a `### <topic>` part per topic; no global notes, sources or dates) between `<!-- BEGIN COMPOSER PLUS MEMORY … -->` and `<!-- END COMPOSER PLUS MEMORY -->` in `AGENTS.md` of the memory's own project folder (from its `project.json`; its real path must still hash to the memory id; the browser never sends a path). Missing markers: the section goes at the end (or a new file); broken markers: 409. The preview is a unified diff, nothing written; **Write AGENTS.md** writes it once (a temp file in the same folder, then one rename), only while AGENTS.md and the notes are as at the preview (409), 30 min. AGENTS.md is read through realpath, only inside the folder, only a regular file, with O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK, at most 512 kB. One memory action at a time. Tether: Project memory sheet → Export to AGENTS.md (`/plus/memory-export`).
- Memory note source link: On by default (browser switch); works while Project memory is on. A note that comes from a chat keeps `[source: <session id> #<seq>]`: memory_remember writes the chat's newest own user message (read with `sessionQuery.observeSession`; a fork starts at `inheritedEventCount`; messages withdrawn by `composer-plus-rollback` or `dsh-rewind` are left out); the review writes the newest user line it read; an accepted suggestion writes the line it came from; a copy keeps the source. The `memory-edit` view gives each note `source: {sessionId, seq?}` (only `session-…` ids; an actor such as `editor` gives none). Open memory → **Source** next to a note closes the dialog and Settings and opens the chat at that message with the Copy message link opener (dsh loads older history first). Tether: a tap on Source in the Project memory sheet opens the chat at the message (`c.openMessage`).
- Copy memory to another project: On by default (browser switch); works while Project memory is on. Open memory → select a project or Global memory → **Copy to project**: a checkbox per note, a search box (case and accents ignored, Enter picks the first match) over dsh's projects (`workspaceRegistry.list()`, A–Z, never a path from the browser). The Host copies the picked notes into the target project's memory in one batch: all or none (a note that does not fit, or a note that is gone, refuses all of them with the reason; files and journal as they were), topic and source kept, a note the target already has skipped, journal actor `copy`, a copy of the target first (Memory version history). At most 100 notes per copy. One memory action at a time. Tether: Project memory sheet → Copy to project (`/plus/memory-copy`).
- Find stale memory notes: On by default (browser switch); works while Project memory is on. When Open memory shows one project (with a folder), the Host checks what its notes name against the project now: file paths in code spans (with "/" or an extension; no URL, absolute path, ".." or glob) by realpath + lstat (never read; a path that leaves the folder is not reported; a path below a dangling symlink is missing, and one odd path does not fail the rest), npm scripts (`npm|pnpm|yarn|bun run X`, `npm test`) from `package.json` read through realpath inside the folder, regular file only, O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK, and branch names (a code span next to the word branch) from one `git for-each-ref` (no path goes to git). A note that names a missing thing shows ⚠ with what is missing, and a summary line. At most 200 things per check. Read-only, no lock, no model call. Checked again when the notes change. Tether: the Project memory sheet shows the same warnings (`/plus/memory-stale`).
- Do not use memory in this chat: On by default (Host switch `memory-chat.json`); works while Project memory is on. A button in the chat header (`conversation.session.header.utilities`) and, on dsh 0.2.1+, on the New chat screen (`conversation.hero.options`) switches the memory off for that chat only. The Host keeps the choice in `$DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-composer-plus/memory-chats.json` (`{off: {<chat id>: <time>}}`, owner-only, newest 500), read before the memory starts. For such a chat (and its subagents, through `parentSession`): the `composer-plus:memory` section renders empty from its next request, the three memory tools leave its tool list (dsh's per-agent `agent.ctx.tools.restrict({deny})`, lifted before the tools go) and refuse when called, and the review sends none of its lines to a model (its cursor still moves, so switching it on later does not send what was said meanwhile). Other chats are not changed. Tether: chat title menu → Use project memory (`/plus/memory-chat`).
- Suggest memory notes from a chat: On by default (browser switch; a model call only on a click); works while Project memory is on, not in a subagent chat or a chat with the memory off. **Suggest for memory** in the chat header: one call to the chat's own model (newest request header, else dsh's default model; no tools; lowest reasoning effort) with the saved notes of the chat's project and the global memory, and the chat's own lines, numbered (a fork starts at `inheritedEventCount`; messages withdrawn by `composer-plus-rollback` or `dsh-rewind` are left out; `/compact` keeps them; at most about 24,000 characters, newest kept). It answers up to 10 suggestions `{text, why, line, global?, topic?}`, cleaned (secret, repeat, saved note, bad topic left out), kept 30 min. **Accept** saves one (journal actor `suggest`, `[source: <chat id> #<seq of its line>]`, a copy first with Memory version history), once; **Reject** stays in the window. One call per chat at a time; accept is one memory action at a time. Tether: chat title menu → Suggest for memory (`/plus/memory-suggest`).
- Allow for this chat: In Auto Review approvals, allow one exact tool in one chat for a set time (Settings: 15 min / 1 h default / 4 h / 8 h / until revoked); then the agent asks again; revocable; saved across restarts.
- Reject with note: Every approval card (dsh's Reject / Allow once) gets "Reject with note…": a field for why, or what to do instead; Reject (or Enter) sends the note as a steer into the waiting turn (dsh's session/prompt, mode steer), then rejects the request, so the next model request holds the rejection result and then the note. A failed note rejects nothing; one rejection per request at a time. No model call of its own, no Host route. In Tether: approval sheet → Reject with note (the same order). On by default.
- Secret input: On by default (no port, no model call; the Host keeps the switch in secrets.json). Every chat gets the tool request_secret({label ≤ 80, purpose? ≤ 300}) (about 870 characters of tool schema per model request). It waits until the user answers in a card on dsh's own row of the call (tool.call.toolview keyed request_secret: label, purpose, a password field, Save, Decline) or in Tether. Save writes the value (≤ 8,192 characters) to $DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-composer-plus/secrets/<32 hex> (folder 0700, file 0600, O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW) and the tool returns only the path with the rule "use it only as input in a shell command". Decline returns "the user did not give this secret"; dsh's Stop ends the wait. A tools/post-execute listener puts [secret] in place of the exact value in each later tool result of that chat; a tools/pre-execute gate denies read, read_image, grep, write, edit and str_replace_editor on the secrets folder (its real path). The files and the in-memory values go when the chat's turn ends and at Host start. Not covered: a shell command that prints the value in another form (base64, a part of it). One open request per chat. A subagent chat gets an error and no card: it stops the step and reports the needed secret to its parent agent. A turn that runs a message that the assistant sent (chat_new or chat_send) gets the same: it reports to the assistant; a later turn that the user typed in that chat opens the card (the next turn is refused too only when the bot did not process the task's turn end: Assistant was off at that turn end, dsh's quit or a parent stop cut the turn, or an outage that Resume takes; with Assistant on, the bot drops a chat_new task at its first turn end). Routes: GET/POST /api/composer-plus.secret-answer (open requests without values; one answer per request), GET/POST {on} /api/composer-plus.secrets (switch). In Tether: a "Secret: <label>" bar above the composer → Enter → a secure field.
- Quote in reply: Select a part of a message (one message text node of the open chat, inside [data-conversation-session=<this chat>]: on dsh 0.2.0/0.2.1 the answer text [data-chat-flow-kind="assistant-step"][data-turn-process-answer="true"] → conversation.chat.node; on dsh 0.2.2+ a [data-text-interaction-source] node: a finished answer, your own message, an open reasoning), then right-click the selected text (a pointer in a box of the range inside that node, or a caret position from document.caretPositionFromPoint that is in the range, as Chromium keeps the selection there: a right-click at once where a mouse drag ended, just past the last selected letter) → a contextmenu listener on document cancels the page menu and opens dsh's Menu primitive at the pointer with two items in the app language (computers.edit.copy, quote.button): Copy (selects the range again and runs document.execCommand('copy'), else dsh's writeClipboard) and Quote (dsh 0.2.2+: dsh's InputActions.insertQuote, the same quote block as dsh's own "Quote text" button, sent as > lines; dsh 0.2.0/0.2.1: InputActions.insertText(captureInsertion()) with > lines and an empty line before and after them; at most 2,000 characters, cut with …; one undo step; a refused insert shows a notice; the composer gets the focus). A right-click on a link or a button, outside the selected text (a pointer outside its boxes whose text position is not in the selection, or the menu key outside the selected message), or with no selection keeps the menu of the browser or the desktop app. Not for tool rows or a selection over two messages. It registers an empty component at key quote, priority -1, of the dsh slot conversation.chat.text-interaction, which hides dsh 0.2.2's floating "Quote text" button while the feature is on. No model call, no Host route. On by default. In Tether: touch and hold an answer → Quote (the whole answer at the end of the field).
- Quote from file preview: Select lines in dsh's file preview in the right sidebar (Workspace files, or a file that the chat opened; text, code, Markdown or PDF viewer of this chat's panel, not full screen) → a floating "Quote" button (document.body, fixed) → at the composer's caret through dsh's InputActions.insertText(captureInsertion()) (one undo step): code and text files `path:from-to` (one line: `path:N`; the line numbers come from the preview's own rows, a triple-click end is not one more line) and the lines in a code block (a longer fence when the lines hold backticks); Markdown files the path and `> ` lines; PDF files `path#page=N` (or N-M) and `> ` lines. The path is relative to the chat's folder when the file is inside it (dsh's `dsh-resource://file/session/<chat>/<path>` address), else absolute. At most 2,000 characters of text (cut with …; the line range stays whole). Not for the path header, another viewer (Excel, Office, images) or a selection over two previews. No model call, no Host route, no file read. On by default. Not in Tether (no file preview on the phone).
- Side chat: Composer button (speech bubbles, conversation.input.right) → the typed plain-text draft (no file chip, attachment or slash command; at most 8,000 characters) becomes a side question: POST /api/composer-plus.side-chat {sessionId, text}. The Host forks the chat with dsh's own sessionController.fork at the newest seq at which no queued (next-turn) or steering (next-step) message waits in the inbox (sideForkSeq), so no waiting message runs in the copy; sets dsh's read-only permission preset (permissionPresets.set, sandbox read-only, approval ask; refused when dsh has no read-only preset), names it "↳ <question>", keeps the chat's model, clears a copied goal, then queues a short English lead and the question. A failed send archives the copy. One start per chat at a time. The side chat opens; a bar above its composer (conversation.input.dock) shows Bring back and Back to the chat. Bring back: GET ?sessionId=<side chat> → the side chat's own messages (after inheritedEventCount; rollback-withdrawn ones left out; only the last reply of each question), each question as a > quote and the answer, at most 12,000 characters, inserted at the parent composer's caret through insertText after the parent opens. Not for subagent chats. One model turn per question; nothing is written to the project. On by default. In Tether: chat title menu → Side chat…; a Bring back bar in the side chat.
- Diff notes: Changes panel (right sidebar) → a file's diff: a + button on each patch row (hover/focus; Shift+click a second row of the same hunk for a range) opens a note field (Enter saves, Shift+Enter new line, Esc cancels). Line numbers come from the hunk headers (the new side, or the old side for removed lines only, marked "(removed)"). The chat's notes are kept per chat in the browser's localStorage (at most 50 notes, 2,000 characters each, 40 lines each) and wait in a bar at the top of the panel; Send to composer inserts them at the chat's composer caret through dsh's InputActions.insertText(captureInsertion()) as Markdown (`path:12-14`, a ```diff block, the note) and removes only the sent notes; a refused insert keeps them. Clear drops them. No model call, no Host route. Needs the changesPanel switch. On by default. In Tether: a file's diff → touch and hold a line → Add note…; the notes show at the top of the Changes sheet; Send puts them after the chat's draft.
- Project status: sidebar project rows show waiting / done / running (an unread finished chat shows its green dot also while another chat runs). In "Workspace Tree", a parent folder's row also counts the chats of the projects inside it (each branch folder).
- Git branch on chat rows: Git branch on chat rows: in the sidebar's "In one list" view, each chat row shows the git branch of the chat's folder at its last turn (the Host records it with read-only git at each turn start and end; no pill for a detached HEAD (no commit id), outside a repository, or before the first turn since install). In "WorkSpace" and "Workspace Tree", no chat row shows it: the chat is already under its project row. Tether shows it only in "In one list" too. The switch is kept by the Host (on by default).
- Mark all as read: a project's "…" menu in the sidebar gets "Mark all as read": one click clears dsh's unread (green) dot of every chat in that project; Tether's dots follow.
- Active projects first: a project moves to the top of the sidebar when one of its chats runs or needs you; the move is saved in dsh's project order.
- Recent projects filter: "Active in the last 2 hours" in the sidebar's view options shows only projects with a chat active in the last 2 hours; a finished chat that was not opened yet keeps its project shown. In "Workspace Tree", a parent folder of an active project stays and chats older than 2 hours hide too.
- Collapse all projects: a sidebar header button, shown while a project is open, closes every open project.
- Order by status: "By status" in the sidebar's Order by puts finished, then running or waiting, then automated chats first in "In one list" (view only).
- Background notifications: OS notification and Dock badge when a chat finishes or really waits for an approval, a question or a plan review; click opens the chat. The body of a finished turn is the first line of its last reply (dsh's turnOutline response), never a reply that is only [quiet]: then it is the plain Finished text. For the assistant chat it is the newest real text of the run from the Host (assistant-status reply), also when the run's last reply is [quiet].
- Open waiting chat when idle: when a chat waits for a question, an approval or a plan review (dsh's orange dot), or finished a turn that nobody opened yet (dsh's green dot), and nobody uses dsh for 30 s, dsh opens that chat; orange chats first, then green ones, the longest-waiting one first in each group. Typing, scrolling, mouse moves, a text selection, an open menu or dialog or a draft in the focused field block it; nothing opens while a waiting chat is on screen; nothing opens while the Assistant chat is open; a chat left unanswered can open again after the next 30 s idle. After it opens a green chat (which clears its dot), the next green one waits for a key, a pointer, the wheel or a touch, then 30 s idle. On by default.
- Next waiting chat: a "Next waiting chat (N)" button in the sidebar header and the dsh command composerPlus.nextWaiting (default Cmd+Shift+E / Ctrl+Shift+E; none on web Linux; editable on dsh's Keyboard shortcuts page) open the next chat that waits for the user, without the chat on screen (a click on the button also finds that chat in the sidebar: a collapsed project opens, the list scrolls to it and its row blinks for 5 s): orange dot first (a question, an approval or a plan review that can be answered here), then green dot (a finished, unread turn), the longest-waiting one first in each group (the same order as Open waiting chat when idle). N counts those chats; the dot of the button has the color of the next one; the button hides at N = 0 and the key answers "No other chat waits for you". Subagent rows and requests that cannot be answered here do not count. In Tether: a button with the dot and N in the Sessions toolbar, and the chat title menu → Next waiting chat (N). On by default.
- Option buttons: when the newest answer of an idle chat ends with an option list (a numbered list of 1–9 items, numbered from 1, under a Markdown heading or bold line "Options", "Choices", "Next steps" or the same words in the 13 languages; the list must be the last block), one button per option shows under that answer (dsh's turn-tail slot) while the composer is empty. While the buttons show, the page hides that answer's numbered option list (dsh's rendered list; the bold heading line "Options:" stays above), so the options show once, as buttons: each button shows the item's first line and its title (tooltip) holds the whole item; when the buttons go (picked, text in the composer, a newer answer) the list shows again. Only the page changes: the chat log, dsh's Copy and other viewers keep the list (Tether also hides it while its buttons show); a numbered list without the heading stays text, and when the list on the page does not match the options (another count) nothing is hidden. A click sends "Option N: <whole item>" through dsh's own send (queue), once; the item marked "(recommended)" is highlighted. A picked answer, an answer withdrawn by Turn rollback or dsh-rewind-plugin, and a fork's inherited answer show no buttons. While buttons show, Next message prediction makes no call. On dsh's question card, keys 1–9 click option N (not in a text field, not with a modifier, not during IME composition, not in the first 800 ms of a question). No model call of its own. In Tether: the same buttons under the newest answer (the same parser rule). In the assistant chat only, a completed news turn whose every text is only [quiet] does not end the older answer's buttons (your message after that answer does). On by default.
- Approve button: On by default (no port, no model call of its own; the Host keeps the switch in approve-button.json). Auto review (aiproxy-review) sees only user messages and tool calls, so an approval sentence must arrive as a user message. While on, every chat gets a short system-prompt section (composer-plus:approve-button): when the agent needs a written approval sentence, it writes the exact sentence in a fenced code block with the info string onay. It writes at most one block in the chat at a time: the pending approvals in one sentence in one block (only the newest block gets a button), and after a user message an approval that is still pending goes again into the next block with any new approval; a reply without a block keeps the button until the user's next message, so a reply to news, a scheduled reminder or an agent result does not write an unchanged block again (a new block only when the pending list changes or after a user message); the block stays at most 500 characters (APPROVAL_MAX, one value in index.js and client.js), always: when the pending approvals do not fit, the block holds the most urgent ones that fit and one short line outside it says how many still wait (they come in the next replies); the sentence names only the targets and the live or not-live scope (no file lines or script names), each by its subject in the user's words, never by an internal code (a review item name, a session id). When the newest onay block of a chat is longer, has such a hold word or is a loose deploy line, the Host adds one hidden note (source composer-plus-approve-long, with the length, the word or the strict line) to the next step of that chat that already carries a message with text (not a Continue or news wake marker, not dsh's runtime context); it never starts a step or a turn. A newer block of the right length, a rollback of the block or the switch off clears it. The record is in memory only, so a dsh restart drops it. The client reads each answer of an idle chat after the user's newest message, also one in the middle of the newest turn or in an earlier turn (a subagent's result or Assistant news can continue the turn, or start a new one, after the answer that asks; dsh shows such a message as a context row, not as the user's). Only the newest of these answers that has an onay block counts (a newer answer without a block keeps it, and so does a newer turn without a text answer (tools only), with the button under that turn's end; an older block gives no second button, also when the newest block gets none). It shows one Approve button per closed, top-level onay block of that answer under the newest turn's end (dsh's turn-tail slot, the same rules and store as Option buttons: not an answer withdrawn by Turn rollback or dsh-rewind-plugin, not a fork's inherited answer, a user message that a rollback withdrew does not count, only while the composer is empty); the same sentence twice gives one button. A click sends the block's exact text (trimmed) through dsh's own conversation.send (queue), once per answer; the button is off during and after the send; a failed send shows the reason. No button for an unclosed, empty, indented or nested block, more than 500 characters, or a character outside printable ASCII, the Turkish letters and a few typographic marks, a hold or stop word of Auto review's deploy gate in a block that names deploy, canlı or yayın after its not-live scope phrases are taken out ("canlı değil", "(canlı) deploy ayrı onayla", "yalnız yerel"; the HOLD list is copied from the Auto review plugin: dur, durdur, bekle, iptal, ertele, vazgeç, hayır, stop, cancel, negated deploy verbs, "deploy/yayın/canlı/başlat/güncelle … yok|olmaz|dokunma"), dur or durdur after a -sA condition in any block ("gerekirse dur", "çıkarsa hemen durdur", "açıksa dur"; not "kadar durdur", "Bursa sayımını durdur"), a negative or revoke form of the Auto review plugin's STOP list (the plugin marks a relayed approval with one as a possible revoke): -masın/-mesin (not before "diye"), -mayın/-meyin, "onaylamıyorum", "onayı geri al" or "onayımı geri al" (not "Onaylıyorum geri alma", "onaylar geri alınınca" or the noun "onayı geri alma özelliği"), and "etme" or "yapma" at the end of a clause (before . , ; ! ) … — –, a line end or the block end; not : ? or a quote mark: "merge etme.", "merge etme, testleri çalıştır.", "(push etme)") in any block ("denemesin", "yapmasın"; not "geri alınsın" or "olmasın diye"; a noun list such as "commit etme, push etme düzeltmeleri" loses the button), and only in a live block one word of a fixed list (kurma, durdurma, yayınlama, gönderme, silme, atma, başlatma, "geri alma", "geri çekme", bırak, kalsın, yok) at the end of a clause ("eski servisi silme, yedek al."; not "silme betiği", and not a list item in another block; a feature name or a fact before , or ) such as "Tur geri alma, …" or "(veri kaybı yok)" loses the button there), or a block that asks for a live deploy ("canlı", "deploy" and a commit SHA, or a block that starts with "CANLI DEPLOY <product>" before a SHA, ŞİMDİ or SAAT) and is not the gate's strict line ("CANLI DEPLOY <PRODUCT> <SHA, 7-40 hex with a letter a-f> ŞİMDİ" or "… SAAT HH:MM", optionally after "Onaylıyorum: ", one final period, nothing after it; any product word, or only the names of the optional deployProducts list in the plugin's config row, for example deployProducts: [shop, acme-web] (the Approve button route gives the list to the client; the prompt rule and the note then name these names in place of <PRODUCT>); index.js and client.js have the same expressions). Otherwise a sentence that names a live or public target (production, a live database, deploy, release, npm publish, a public PR) gets a button too. The prompt rule asks for positive scope words ("canlı değil", "yalnız yerel", "deploy ayrı onayla") and the strict deploy line. The sentence shows once: while its button shows, dsh's code block of that sentence is hidden (the button holds the whole sentence); every other onay block with a sentence that could get a button (sent, answered, an older block, or its button hidden while the chat runs or the composer has text) shows as plain gray text without the code header. A block that can never get a button stays dsh's code block. Only the page changes (an attribute and CSS on dsh's .md-code-block): the chat log, dsh's Copy (the answer's Markdown) and other viewers keep the block. Messages already in the chat are not changed; user messages never get a button. In the assistant chat, while the status panel shows (the card stack, feature assistantTodos), the button is only in the Approval card of the stack (the same store, send path and guard) and the sentence stays in the reply as gray text; with no stack (the panel off, a dsh update that renamed data-conversation-content) the button is under the reply again, and every other chat keeps it under the reply. Tether shows the same button with the same rule (a shared test table, test/fixtures/approval-blocks.json); a tap asks once and sends the exact sentence as your message; its words follow the language that the gateway gives in /me (lang).
- Application language: Switches the whole dsh interface to one of 11 extra languages: Türkçe, Español, Português (Brasil), Français, Deutsch, Русский, 日本語, 한국어, Bahasa Indonesia, Tiếng Việt, हिन्दी. Each pack has 5,541 texts: every UI text of dsh 0.2.2-rc.5, the plugin's own texts and the dsh-rewind plugin.
- Mobile connect (iPhone): use dsh from the Tether iPhone app on the same Wi-Fi or over Tailscale. Switch it on in Settings → Composer Plus (off by default, it opens a network port on the Mac); a "Mobile connect" button at the bottom left shows the pairing QR code (a tether://pair link: the iPhone Camera opens it in Tether, which asks before it connects; the Mac page shows the request, a countdown and what happened). Pinned TLS, one-time pairing code approved on the Mac, hashed device tokens, RPC allowlist. The phone keeps any number of paired Macs and switches between them from a picker at the top; only the Mac on screen is connected. The Mac pairing page lists each paired iPhone with its last connection and removes one with one click (its key stops working at once); a "Tailscale only" option refuses local-network connections; an access log shows each connection attempt (time, IP, device, allowed or refused). Tether can lock itself with Face ID or the passcode (Tether Settings → Privacy). A message from the phone can carry photos from the camera, the photo library or the clipboard (the composer's + menu; at most 4, sent as JPEG attachments of the message). The iOS app source is in tether/ios. Tether's green dots (unread finished chats) and its Sessions count are the same as dsh's, both ways: the Host keeps one list, dsh's window reports its reads and its dots to it and clears dsh's dot of a chat read on a phone (checked every 3 s); archived chats get no dot; a Mac without this list shows no green dots in Tether.
- Remote computers: open the dsh of your other Macs over Tailscale and use them in the same dsh window, from a computer picker in the left sidebar (under the brand, above New session). Off by default (it opens network ports). The Mac to open switches on "Let other computers open this Mac" (a front door on its Tailscale address only, pinned TLS, one-time pairing link, Approve on that Mac, hashed tokens); the other Mac pastes its link and gives it a name that differs from This Mac and the other computers. The picked computer fills the window (a desktop webview or a web iframe) through a loopback relay with a one-time ticket; this Mac keeps running behind it. With exactly one other computer, the picker has two parts, "This Mac | <name>", the one on screen highlighted, and one click on the other part switches (no menu); a right-click opens the whole menu (Add a computer…). With more computers, the picker opens a menu and says "Back to this Mac" while a computer shows. Over a page without its own picker (an older Composer Plus there), this Mac’s picker shows in the same place. A paired computer gets full control of dsh on the opened Mac. In the desktop webview, dsh refuses the page the clipboard permission; Composer Plus adds a fallback to that page so that a failed navigator.clipboard.writeText copies the same text through the page's copy command; a single text/plain navigator.clipboard.write (dsh 0.2.2's Copy Session as Markdown) takes the same path (text only, within Chromium's 5-second click activation; image copy, paste buttons and a copy whose text takes longer still fail there).
- Automatic updates: at dsh start, installs the newest GitHub release (once it is on npm, as its exact npm tarball) through dsh's own plugin manager and notifies; dsh 0.2.1 loads it at once when no dsh settings change, otherwise restart dsh to load it. The first start that runs the installed version shows its release notes once in a closable "What's new" window, in the UI language (Application language): the notes ship with the package in 13 languages (release-notes.json, no extra network call); a language without notes shows the English notes. A line below the notes asks for a GitHub star at most once in 30 days (no network call), never again after its link or "Do not ask again". The window also shows after an update through any path (Settings → Plugins, a copied folder), once per new version, not at the first install; "What’s new in this version" in the update row opens it again. When the version on disk is newer than the running copy, the row asks to restart dsh.
- On/off filter: On by default (browser switch, no Host route). Settings → Composer Plus shows **All**, **On** and **Off** next to the feature search (a `role="group"` of buttons with `aria-pressed`). A row's state is its own switch value (`isOn` of the merged toggles, Host switches included); search and filter both apply. A row switched while On or Off is picked stays until a filter is picked again (the focus stays on its switch). On and Off hide the language and update rows. The choice is not saved. Switching it off hides the buttons and shows every row.
- Category filter: On by default (browser switch, no Host route). Settings → Composer Plus shows a **Category** menu next to the feature search and the All / On / Off buttons (a button with `aria-haspopup="menu"` that opens dsh's own menu). **All** (the default) shows every row; each of the 8 categories (Sidebar and chat list, Composer and queue, Chat view, Approvals and safety, Agent skills, Assistant and task board, Project memory, App, devices and backup) shows only its features, in Settings order. Each feature is in exactly one category; the language and update rows are in App, devices and backup. Category, On/off filter and search all apply. The filter only hides rows: no switch value changes, and the choice is not saved. Switching it off hides the menu and shows every row.
- Report an issue: On by default (a model call and gh only on a click). Settings → Composer Plus → Report an issue… (under the intro) or a chat's … menu → Report a Composer Plus issue…: a panel with five types (Bug, Feature request, Improvement, Translation, Question) and a text field. Write draft sends only the type and the text (not the chat or the project) to dsh's default model in one call (`POST /api/composer-plus.issue-report {type, text}`); the model writes an English title and a Markdown body with the type's sections (bug: What happened, Steps to reproduce, Expected, Actual; feature: Problem, Proposed solution, Alternatives; improvement: Current behavior, Suggested change, Why; translation: Language, Where, Current text, Suggested text; question: Question, Context) and is told not to invent facts; the Host adds the type's title prefix ([Bug], [Feature request], [Improvement], [Translation], [Question]) and a line with the Composer Plus, dsh and OS versions, and replaces the home folder path with `~`. The user edits the draft; Open issue (`{title, body, open: true}`) runs the user's own `gh issue create --repo=furkancak1r/dsh-composer-plus` (body on stdin, the gh login of the Mac, at most 60 s) and shows the issue link. Text that looks like a key, token or password is refused; one open at a time (409); the same title and body again within an hour answers the earlier issue instead of a copy. When gh fails, Open on GitHub instead opens `https://github.com/furkancak1r/dsh-composer-plus/issues/new` with the title and body filled in. Tether: Settings → Report a Composer Plus issue.
- Backup: On by default (nothing runs without a click). Settings → Composer Plus → Backup: Back up now writes the whole dsh home into <dsh home>/backups/dsh-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSSmmm>.tar.gz (default ~/.dsh/backups; COMPOSER_PLUS_BACKUP_DIR overrides it) (gzip tar, one top folder) with .sha256, .meta.json and .redacted.json; the format is the same as dsh-backup 0.13, so its archives work when they are in that folder. Up to 1.29.2 the folder was ~/Desktop/dsh-backups: Composer Plus never moves or deletes it and does not list its archives; a start and each backup only replace the rescue console there (when it is there, also with Rescue console off), so that its restore also keeps <dsh home>/backups. dsh-backup 0.13 archives the whole dsh home (its exclude list is empty by default), so it must be removed or get `backups` in its exclude list. cache/, dsh-runtimes/, backups/, every node_modules and .system are not archived. Masked (not in the archive, the real copy only in composer-plus-vault/<archive>/ of the backup folder, 0600; dsh-backup archives read their secrets from its vault/ mirror): .credentials.yaml, .env and .env.*, *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx, qq-bridge/config.json, and in every .yml/.yaml file (also cordis.patch.yml.bak-…) the values (one line, plain or block scalar) of keys whose last word is token, secret, password, passphrase, credential(s), authorization, apiKey, accessKey, secretKey, privateKey, clientSecret, authKey or authToken (maxTokens and apiKeyEnv stay). Symbolic links are archived as links and never followed; FIFOs, sockets and devices are skipped; files are read with O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK. Per archive: Check (reads it fully, checksum, safe names), For another computer (a transfer-<time> folder with the archive, its sidecars and the rescue console, no vault: secrets are entered again there), Delete (also its vault copies). One backup action at a time (also against the rescue console: a lock file in the folder). Restore is not in dsh: quit dsh and use the rescue console. Not in Tether.
- Automatic backup: Off by default (each copy is about the size of the dsh home without its cache; the Host keeps the switch in auto-backup.json). When on, the Host backs up every 6, 12, 24 (default), 72 or 168 hours, counted from the newest full backup in the folder (also a manual one), and keeps the newest 3, 5, 7 (default) or 14 of its own automatic backups (Back up now deletes nothing; dsh-backup archives are never deleted); never in the first 45 s after a start. Keep 2 (while the switch is on) counts every Composer Plus archive together: automatic, snapshot and Back up now; the next automatic backup is due one interval after the newest backup or snapshot, so after an upgrade the last full backup from before it stays with the snapshot. Each new archive is written with fsync and first read back in full against its checksum; only then do older ones go (with their sidecars and composer-plus-vault copies) until the newest 2 stay, so while it runs the disk needs room for a third. The new one is never deleted (with any Keep). A failed or cancelled backup deletes nothing (a name that is already in the folder is refused before anything is written); an old archive that cannot be deleted stays (logged, and Settings says how many) and goes with the next backup. When dsh or Composer Plus starts with another version than at the last start, it first takes a dsh-pre-upgrade-<time> snapshot (the newest 2 stay). A failed backup shows in Settings and the next try waits 30 minutes (or the interval when shorter). Not in Tether.
- Session log check: On by default (runs only on a click). Settings → Composer Plus → Session log check → Check session logs reads the newest log of every chat under sessions/ (session[.vN].jsonl[.zstd]): zstd frames with dsh's own rules (a torn last frame is not damage: dsh cuts it at its next write), the first frame must be exactly the header line, no record may end inside a complete frame, and a row that is not JSON or (v4) has a seq other than its place is damage only when a turn/end row follows it (dsh's own recoverable rule; otherwise dsh opens the rows before it). Repair from backups checks again, then puts back each damaged log of a chat that is not open in this dsh from the newest archive that has a healthy copy; the damaged file stays as <name>.corrupt-<time>. Messages after that backup are not in the copy. Open chats: the rescue console, with dsh closed. Not in Tether.
- Rescue console: On by default (the Host keeps the switch in rescue-console.json). Each backup writes composer-plus-rescue.mjs (the same backup.mjs, Node standard library only) and a launcher (macOS: Composer Plus Rescue.command, Linux: composer-plus-rescue.sh, Windows: Composer Plus Rescue.cmd) into the backup folder; a start replaces a copy that is there. The launcher finds Node.js 18 or later on PATH, Homebrew, nvm or dsh's own runtime, else runs the DeepSeek Harness app as Node.js (ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1). The Windows launcher starts Node.js from the user folder: Windows does not rename a folder that a window is in. A terminal menu, no network port: list backups, check one, restore one, check session logs, repair them. Restore and repair refuse while dsh runs (storages/dsh-composer-plus/running/host-<pid>.json of a live process; each dsh process has its own), checks the archive, asks to type RESTORE, writes it into a new folder next to the dsh home (files O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW, symbolic links last and never followed, no entry below a link, no devices), puts the masked files back from the vault (composer-plus-vault/<archive>/, or dsh-backup's vault/ mirror for its archives), swaps the folders (the old home stays as <home>.pre-restore-<time>), moves cache/, dsh-runtimes/, backups/ (also the console's own folder when it is in the dsh home) and node_modules over from it (a backup folder that it cannot move back stays there: the console names it and does not tell you to remove the old home), and offers pnpm install for profiles that need it. Switched off, the files are removed. Not in Tether.
<!-- END GENERATED FEATURES -->
